section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what age can a New Mexico teen apply for a learner's permit?
options: a:14,b:14 and a half,c:15,d:16
note: New Mexico allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 15. A parent or guardian must sign the application, and the permit allows supervised driving practice under New Mexico's GDL program.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the passing score for the New Mexico MVD knowledge test?
options: a:70% (18/25 correct),b:72% (18/25 correct),c:80% (20/25 correct),d:85% (21/25 correct)
note: New Mexico requires a passing score of 72% on the 25-question knowledge test, which means you must answer at least 18 out of 25 questions correctly. This is a lower passing threshold than most states, which typically require 80%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in New Mexico?
note: New Mexico sets the per se DWI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit. Reaching 0.08% BAC is sufficient for a DWI charge regardless of apparent impairment. Note: New Mexico uses 'DWI' not 'DUI.'

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: New Mexico's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 sets the illegal BAC at:
options: a:0.00% — any detectable amount,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: New Mexico's zero tolerance law sets the underage DWI threshold at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21. Drivers under 21 found with a BAC of 0.02% or higher face automatic license revocation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in New Mexico and encounter a dust storm (haboob) that reduces visibility to near zero. What should you do?
options: a:Turn on high beams and slow to 15 mph,b:Pull off the road completely, turn off lights, and wait for the storm to pass,c:Continue at reduced speed — dust storms pass quickly,d:Use your hazard lights and stop on the shoulder
note: In a severe dust storm, pull completely off the paved road, turn off your headlights (so other drivers do not follow them into a stopped vehicle), set the parking brake, and wait for the storm to pass. This is critical in New Mexico's desert regions where haboobs can reduce visibility to zero.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on a New Mexico rural highway when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: New Mexico's default speed limit on rural highways is 55 mph when no posted sign indicates otherwise. On divided four-lane highways, the default may be higher. Always check posted signs — New Mexico has some roads with limits up to 75 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In New Mexico, when must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only at marked crosswalks with signals,b:At all crosswalks — marked and unmarked — and anytime a pedestrian is in your path,c:Only when a pedestrian is on the same side of the road as you,d:Only at intersections with traffic signals
note: New Mexico requires drivers to yield to pedestrians at all crosswalks, both marked and unmarked, and any time a pedestrian is in the roadway. An unmarked crosswalk exists at every intersection — even without painted lines — where two public streets meet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does New Mexico's Move Over law require when passing a stopped emergency vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Move over only for police vehicles, not for tow trucks,b:Move one lane away from any stopped emergency or highway maintenance vehicle — or slow if lane change is unsafe,c:Stop completely behind the emergency vehicle,d:Maintain your lane — emergency vehicles have protective barriers
note: New Mexico's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights. If moving is not safely possible, reduce speed to at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a New Mexico two-lane highway, you see a broken yellow center line on your side of the road. This means:
options: a:Passing is always prohibited,b:Passing is permitted when it is safe and the road ahead is clear,c:You must slow to 45 mph before passing,d:Passing is only permitted by the vehicle ahead, not you
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line on your side of the center allows passing when you have adequate sight distance, no oncoming traffic, and can complete the pass safely. A solid yellow line on your side prohibits passing — never cross a solid line on your side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must all drivers do when approaching a school bus with flashing red lights on an undivided New Mexico road?
options: a:Stop only if driving behind the bus,b:All traffic in both directions must stop at least 10 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and pass the bus carefully,d:Stop only if children are visible near the bus
note: New Mexico requires all traffic on an undivided road in both directions to stop when a school bus activates its flashing red lights and stop arm. Stop at least 10 feet from the bus and wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in a New Mexico school zone when children are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: New Mexico school zones have a 15–20 mph speed limit when children are present or when warning lights are flashing. Specific limits are posted at each school zone. Always watch for school zone signs, especially during arrival and dismissal times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under New Mexico's implied consent law, refusing a chemical test after a DWI arrest results in:
options: a:No penalty — you have the right to refuse,b:Automatic license revocation for at least 1 year for a first offense,c:Only a fine with no license action,d:License revocation only if convicted of DWI
note: New Mexico's implied consent law means driving on state roads implies your consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in an automatic license revocation of at least 1 year, plus the refusal can be used as evidence in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a New Mexico highway and notice the front end of your vehicle drifting slightly. This may indicate:
options: a:Your speed is too low — accelerate to correct the drift,b:A flat or underinflated tire, alignment issue, or loose suspension component,c:Normal driving on desert roads — wind causes all vehicles to drift,d:An engine problem — turn off the ignition immediately
note: Drifting or pulling to one side while driving can indicate an underinflated or flat tire, alignment problems, or a loose suspension component. In New Mexico's desert heat, tire pressure changes rapidly. Pull over safely and inspect your tires before continuing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are headlights required in New Mexico?
options: a:Only between midnight and 5 AM,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and in weather that reduces visibility,c:Only when driving on highways,d:Only in rain or fog
note: New Mexico requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and whenever weather conditions reduce visibility. In New Mexico's desert, sudden rain and dust storms can significantly reduce visibility — turn your headlights on any time visibility is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal at a New Mexico intersection mean?
options: a:Stop completely and wait for the light to turn green,b:Yield to all traffic and then proceed,c:Slow down, be alert, and proceed with caution,d:Proceed without slowing — it is just a cautionary signal
note: A flashing yellow signal means caution — reduce speed, look carefully for crossing traffic, and proceed when it is safe. A full stop is not required (unlike a flashing red), but you must be prepared to yield if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum recommended following distance on New Mexico highways?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: New Mexico recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On desert highways where blowing dust, flash floods, and wildlife can suddenly appear, consider increasing to 4 seconds or more for a safer buffer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: New Mexico has many open range areas. If you hit livestock on an open range road, who is generally responsible?
options: a:The livestock owner is always responsible for animals on the road,b:The driver may be responsible — in open range areas, animals have the right to be on the road,c:The state highway department is responsible for all livestock incidents,d:Neither party is legally responsible — it is treated as an act of nature
note: In New Mexico's open range areas, drivers must watch for livestock. In open range jurisdictions, ranchers are not required to fence in their animals — the animals have the right to be on the road. Drivers are expected to drive at a safe speed and watch for animals, especially at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are making a left turn at an intersection. An oncoming vehicle is approaching. When should you turn?
options: a:Turn immediately — your turn signal gives you the right of way,b:Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic before turning,c:Flash your lights to signal the oncoming driver to slow,d:Turn if the oncoming vehicle is more than 5 car lengths away
note: A vehicle turning left must always yield to oncoming traffic. Wait for a safe gap — one large enough to complete the turn without forcing oncoming drivers to brake. Misjudging the speed of oncoming traffic is a leading cause of left-turn crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What shape and color identifies a regulatory sign in New Mexico?
options: a:Yellow diamond,b:Orange pentagon,c:White rectangle or special shapes (octagon for stop, triangle for yield),d:Green rectangle
note: Regulatory signs are white rectangles or special shapes like the red octagonal stop sign and triangular yield sign. These signs communicate laws you must obey — speed limits, no passing, do not enter, and similar requirements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under New Mexico GDL rules, what restriction applies to drivers under 18 regarding nighttime driving?
options: a:No driving between midnight and 5:00 AM,b:No driving between 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM,c:No driving between 10:00 PM and 5:00 AM,d:No driving between midnight and 6:00 AM
note: Under New Mexico's GDL program, provisional license holders (under 18) are prohibited from driving between midnight and 5:00 AM, unless accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older, or driving for work, school, religious activities, or emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In New Mexico, when is it legal to make a U-turn?
options: a:Anywhere as long as you signal first,b:Where permitted by signs and where you have adequate sight distance in both directions,c:Only at designated U-turn lanes,d:U-turns are prohibited statewide in New Mexico
note: U-turns are legal in New Mexico where signs permit them and where you have clear visibility of at least 500 feet in both directions. U-turns are prohibited near the crest of a hill, on a curve, at railroad crossings, and where signs prohibit them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal mean in New Mexico?
options: a:You may proceed in the direction of the arrow if the intersection is clear,b:You must stop and may not proceed in the direction of the arrow until the signal changes,c:Yield to pedestrians and then proceed in the direction of the arrow,d:The arrow indicates the lane is closing in that direction
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and may not move in the direction of the arrow. Unlike a round red light (where a right turn may be permitted after stopping), a red arrow prohibits movement in that direction regardless of other traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Flash flooding is a serious hazard on New Mexico roads. What should you do if you encounter a flooded road?
options: a:Drive through at low speed if the water looks shallow,b:Turn around — do not attempt to drive through flood water,c:Increase speed to cross quickly before the water rises,d:Park on the road's edge and wait for the water to recede
note: New Mexico's 'Turn Around, Don't Drown' principle is critically important — even 6 inches of water can cause a loss of vehicle control, and 12 inches can carry away a small car. Flash floods are common and appear quickly on New Mexico desert roads. Never attempt to cross a flooded road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing with no gates, lights, or signs other than an 'RR' pavement marking, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed — unmarked crossings are rarely active,b:Slow to 15 mph, look and listen for approaching trains, and stop if one is coming,c:Stop completely for 30 seconds before crossing,d:Honk your horn and proceed carefully
note: At any railroad crossing in New Mexico — even with minimal markings — slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Trains cannot stop quickly. If a train is approaching, stop completely. Never race a train to a crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the purpose of a shared center turn lane on a New Mexico road?
options: a:For passing slow vehicles in either direction,b:For vehicles from either direction to use while waiting to make a left turn,c:For emergency vehicles and buses only,d:For cyclists and pedestrians to cross safely
note: A shared center turn lane — marked with yellow lines and arrows pointing both ways — is used by vehicles from both directions to slow down and wait while making a left turn. Do not use it as a travel lane or for passing. Enter the lane only when close to your intended turn.

question: If you plan to pass a pedestrian on the roadway but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Maintain your speed and pass quickly.,c:Honk to make the pedestrian move over.,d:Pass the pedestrian before the oncoming vehicle arrives.
note: When you have a pedestrian ahead and an oncoming vehicle, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Once the lane is clear and you have enough room, pass the pedestrian at a safe speed and distance.

question: When should you use low-beam headlights?
options: a:On a well-lit street at night.,b:Only when an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on.,c:In fog.
note: Use low‑beam headlights in fog because high beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams give better visibility in fog, heavy rain, or snow and help other drivers see you without blinding them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. It is not treated like a slow or yield sign.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They require wider turns and need more stopping distance.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.,d:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight, and they also require more space to turn. You should give them extra room and never assume they can stop quickly, even if they have powerful brakes.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do before moving over?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Glance over your shoulder and signal at least 100 feet in residential areas.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, signal in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas), check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps ensure there is no vehicle or cyclist in the lane you plan to enter.

question: What is the usual effect of driving while distracted by other activities?
options: a:It is never dangerous.,b:It makes drivers faster to respond.,c:Drivers react more slowly to hazards.
note: Distractions such as phones, eating, or adjusting controls take your attention away from the road. When you are distracted, you notice hazards later and react more slowly, which greatly increases your chances of being involved in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do functioning brake lights tell other drivers?
options: a:Are changing lanes.,b:Are making a turn.,c:Have your emergency brake on.,d:Are slowing down or stopping.
note: When you press the brake pedal, your brake lights come on to warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This advance warning helps them adjust their speed and following distance to avoid rear-end collisions.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what is the hand signal indicating?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Slow down only.,d:Stop.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward means a right turn, and a left arm pointed downward means the driver is stopping or slowing sharply. When you see an arm pointed down, be ready to slow or stop.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,d:Only before passing.
note: Good drivers scan all around their vehicle, not just straight ahead. Checking your mirrors often—about every few seconds—helps you know what traffic is doing behind and beside you so you can change lanes, slow, or stop more safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do on a green arrow signal?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.,b:Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles that are already in the intersection. Once the way is clear, you may complete your turn without waiting a set number of seconds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which passing actions are unlawful?
options: a:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Both of the above.,c:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone.
note: Passing is illegal both in marked no‑passing zones and at railroad crossings. You must not cross the centerline to pass where there are solid yellow lines, no‑passing signs, limited sight distance (hills/curves), intersections, or railroad crossings, because oncoming traffic or trains may not be visible in time to stop safely.

question: When should you reduce your speed below the posted limit?
options: a:Never; always follow the posted limit.,b:Whenever conditions require it,c:Only when police direct you to do so.
note: Posted speed limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit whenever rain, snow, ice, fog, heavy traffic, poor visibility, or road hazards make the posted speed unsafe. Driving at the limit can still be illegal if conditions require a lower speed to be safe.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the vehicle and because the driver may not see you.,b:Because you will be caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,c:Because it will save fuel.
note: Large trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and have large blind spots directly behind them. By increasing your following distance, you improve your ability to see traffic and hazards ahead and make it more likely the truck driver can see you, giving both of you more time to react.

question: How should you expect children to behave when driving in areas where they play?
options: a:To stop at the curb before crossing.,b:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,c:To run out in front of you without looking.
note: You should assume children near the road may act unpredictably, such as running into the street without looking. Because children often do not judge speed or distance well, you must slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop at any moment rather than expecting them to behave safely.

question: What is the correct response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid heavy braking until the vehicle has slowed.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: In a tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking until the vehicle has slowed, because sudden braking can cause loss of control, especially if a front tire has blown. Steer smoothly to a safe place off the road.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,c:Lanes moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A solid line down the center of a two‑lane road is always yellow, not white, and it separates traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid yellow centerline means you may not cross it to pass because it is unsafe to do so. Solid white lines are used between lanes moving in the same direction, usually at the edge of the road or to discourage lane changes, not in the center of a two‑lane two‑way road.

question: To reduce headlight glare at night from oncoming vehicles, where should you look?
options: a:At the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,c:Straight at the headlights.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using the painted edge line or curb as a guide. This keeps you in your lane while protecting your eyes from being blinded by the bright lights. Never stare directly into oncoming headlights.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your high beams repeatedly.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull alongside and yell at the driver.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and create space instead of reacting aggressively. Aggressive responses like flashing high beams, honking excessively, or yelling can escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash. Your priority is to maintain a safe following distance and keep control of your vehicle.

question: After a train has passed at a crossing, what should you do before driving on?
options: a:Drive immediately if the first train is clear.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.,d:Do both — look for another train and wait until signals stop.
note: After a train passes, you must make sure the crossing is completely clear and that no other train is coming before you proceed. Look carefully for a second train on any track, and do not drive forward until all warning devices—such as flashing lights and lowered gates—have fully stopped and the gates are raised. Trains can approach quickly and quietly, so you must confirm that all signals indicate it is safe to cross.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Shift into neutral to coast through the water.,b:Maintain posted speed to get through quickly.,c:Avoid it if possible or drive slowly through shallow water
note: If you see a deep puddle, the safest choice is to avoid driving through it because you cannot tell how deep it is or what hazards are hidden under the water. If you must go through standing water that you know is shallow, slow down, drive straight at a steady, low speed, and avoid sudden braking or steering to reduce the risk of skidding or hydroplaning.

question: What is important to remember about wet pavement and the start of rain?
options: a:You need less stopping distance when wet.,b:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning.,c:Roads are especially slippery just after it starts to rain.
note: Roads are most slippery at the beginning of a rainstorm because water mixes with oil, grease, and dust on the surface. This creates a slick film that reduces traction. Slow down, increase following distance, and brake gently to avoid skidding or hydroplaning.

question: If you are involved in an accident, which action is appropriate?
options: a:Stop and move your vehicle out of traffic if possible,b:Drive to the nearest hospital immediately if anyone is injured.,c:Leave the scene if damage is minor.,d:Call the police without stopping.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop immediately, stay at the scene, and, if the vehicles are drivable, move them out of traffic when it is safe to do so. Then check for injuries, call 911 or law enforcement as needed, and exchange information. Leaving the scene is illegal, and you should not drive away to a hospital without stopping and reporting the crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Select a safe gap and merge into traffic.
note: When using an entrance ramp to merge onto an interstate, use the ramp to reach the speed of traffic if possible, check mirrors and blind spots, and choose a safe gap. Merge smoothly into the flow of traffic without stopping unless traffic or conditions force you to stop. Never cross multiple lanes at once when entering.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the steering wheel sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Apply the brakes hard and then steer quickly.,d:Accelerate to regain pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. Ease off the accelerator and brake gently to slow down. Do not jerk the wheel back onto the road. When your speed is under control and there is a safe gap, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly both directions.,b:Never; it is illegal to drive around lowered gates.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through lowered railroad crossing gates. Even if you do not see a train, another train may be approaching or the warning system may still be active. Wait until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and you have checked that the tracks are clear before crossing.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:The driver should honk their horn.,b:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,c:No special action is required.
note: When you see an animal on or near the roadway, slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass very cautiously so you do not startle it into your path or another lane. Sudden horn use can cause the animal to bolt unpredictably and increase the risk of a crash.

question: If you pass your interstate exit, the correct action is to:
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.,d:Make a U-turn through the median.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop, back up on the shoulder, cut across lanes, or make a U-turn through the median, because these maneuvers are illegal and extremely dangerous at freeway speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck will always match posted speed,b:You may not be able to legally pass only if signs say so.,c:The truck may travel slower than the posted speed limit
note: Large trucks often slow down on uphill grades because of their weight and engine limits, so you should expect them to travel below the posted speed limit. Approach with caution, allow extra following distance, and only pass when it is legal and you have enough clear sight distance.

question: When should you increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When driving more slowly than the posted limit.,c:When you are being tailgated.
note: When another driver is following too closely (tailgating), increase the space in front of your vehicle. This larger cushion gives you more time to brake gently and reduces the chance of a rear-end collision if you must slow or stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The exact safe speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a target speed you must always reach. You must slow down below the limit when road, traffic, or weather conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at an upcoming corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:All approaching vehicles and pedestrians with the right-of-way.,b:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a 'Walk' signal.,c:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
note: When turning left, you must yield to all oncoming traffic and to any pedestrians or other road users who have the right‑of‑way. This includes vehicles coming straight through the intersection, vehicles close enough to be a hazard, and pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk. You may only complete your left turn when it is safe and you will not interfere with others who have the right‑of‑way.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk?
options: a:50 feet,b:10 feet,c:25 feet
note: Parking too close to a crosswalk blocks visibility and creates a hazard for pedestrians and drivers. Many states prohibit parking within 25 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection so that drivers can clearly see people entering the crosswalk and have time to stop.

question: What should you do to reduce the chance of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as in dry conditions.,b:Slow down and drive more slowly than in ideal conditions.,c:Drive through deep water at higher speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a film of water and lose contact with the road, causing a loss of steering and braking control. To reduce this risk, you should slow down in wet conditions, especially when water is pooling on the road, and avoid sudden steering or braking.

question: What does a solid white edge line that angles toward the center of the roadway indicate?
options: a:An intersection is just ahead.,b:A mandatory left turn ahead.,c:The road narrows ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the travel lane. When this line angles or slants toward the center of the road, it warns that the usable roadway is narrowing ahead. You should adjust your speed and lane position to stay safely within the lane as the road narrows.

question: Double solid yellow center lines on the roadway indicate:
options: a:A railroad crossing ahead.,b:A pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:No passing is permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a permitted left turn, such as turning into or out of a driveway or side road, when it is safe to do so.

question: You should not enter railroad tracks unless you can clear them completely so your entire vehicle fits on the far side:
options: a:Only when lights are flashing,b:True,c:False,d:Only at marked crossings
note: You must never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. If traffic is stopped ahead, wait before the tracks until you are sure you can cross completely without stopping on them.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They do not need extra room to maneuver.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all sides and need more distance to turn, change lanes, and stop because of their size and weight. Give them extra space and avoid driving alongside them in their blind spots.

question: When the center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, it means:
options: a:You must always stay in your lane.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You may only make right turns from this lane.,d:You are in a passing zone and may pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may cross it to pass if it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic. The solid yellow line on the other side means vehicles in that lane may not pass from their side.

question: When preparing to pass a motorcycle, what must you do regarding lane position?
options: a:Stay in the right lane and crowd the motorcycle.,b:Blow your horn to force the motorcycle onto the shoulder.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane when passing and allow a full lane width to the motorcycle.
note: When passing a motorcycle, move fully into the left lane and treat the motorcycle like any other vehicle, giving it a full lane width. Never crowd or share a lane with a motorcycle, and return to your lane only when you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you near an intersection, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Brake sharply in the center of the intersection.
note: A yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and help you maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself; just apply firm, steady pressure and steer where you want to go.

question: At what speed should you travel relative to others on the road?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At or below the speed limit, adjusted for conditions.
note: You must always adjust your speed to match road, traffic, and weather conditions, while never exceeding the posted speed limit. Sometimes this means driving slower than the speed limit if conditions are poor. Matching the exact speed of surrounding traffic is not always safe or legal if they are going too fast.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, where should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,b:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,c:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
note: When you have hazards on both sides—oncoming traffic to the left and parked cars to the right—steer a middle course. This gives you the most space from both dangers and reduces the risk of sideswiping parked cars or drifting into oncoming traffic.

question: Orange-colored roadway signs are used to indicate:
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:Work zones.,c:School zones.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in construction and maintenance work zones. They warn you of workers, equipment, lane shifts, and other changes, so you should slow down and be prepared for unexpected conditions.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop unless another sign or signal requires it, or conditions ahead make it unsafe to continue at your current speed.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street rather than in a crosswalk, you:
options: a:May proceed without yielding.,b:Can speed up to pass before they reach your lane.,c:Must stop for them.,d:Should honk to make them move.
note: Drivers must always exercise due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when they are crossing illegally. If pedestrians are in your path, you must be prepared to slow or stop to avoid a collision, rather than trying to force them out of the way.

question: Highway signs that warn of potentially hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Guide signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Warning signs.,d:Information signs.
note: Warning signs are typically yellow and are used to alert drivers to conditions ahead that may require slowing down or extra caution, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width.

question: When should you drive in a reversible lane that displays a red X above it?
options: a:When there is no visible oncoming traffic.,b:Never.,c:Only during rush hour.,d:To pass a slow vehicle
note: A red X over a reversible lane means that lane is closed to traffic in your direction. You must never drive in, enter, or use that lane while the red X is displayed, even if it appears clear.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must allow for:
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,d:Larger vehicles can stop quicker in emergencies.
note: Heavy trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop. Leave extra following distance, avoid cutting in front of them, and remember they also make wider turns and have larger blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection requires the same action as what sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any traffic and pedestrians with the right‑of‑way.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway where you are driving, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Slow down and pass with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,d:Continue at the same speed.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass with great caution. Pedestrians can move unpredictably into the lane, so reducing speed gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: Do large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them?
options: a:False — they have small blind spots.,b:True — they can have blind spots that extend far behind.
note: Large trucks and buses have very large blind spots directly behind them that can extend about 200 feet or more. If you follow too closely, the driver may not see you at all, so always leave extra space behind large vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right first.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of the space you want to occupy.,c:Turn your wheels sharply to the left immediately.
note: To begin parallel parking, first pull up so your vehicle is alongside and even with the car in front of the space. Stopping in this position gives you the correct angle and space to back into the spot safely while steering.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Locking of the front wheels and loss of steering control.,b:Faster stopping without skidding.,c:Prevention of brake freezing.
note: On ice or snow, hard continuous braking can cause your wheels to lock, which makes you lose steering control and can lead to a skid. Instead, slow down early and brake gently and gradually so the tires can maintain traction.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you get into the car.,b:Before you start driving.,c:Whenever you need to use them while driving.
note: Adjust your seat, rearview mirror, and side mirrors before you start driving so you have a clear view around your vehicle. Making these adjustments while moving takes your attention from the road and increases crash risk.

question: If it begins to rain while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Turn off headlights to prevent glare.,b:Slow down.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,d:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
note: When it starts to rain, the road becomes especially slippery, so you should slow down, turn on your headlights, and increase your following distance. Driving at the maximum posted speed or faster than traffic in the rain is unsafe because stopping distances increase and traction is reduced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light requires you to:
options: a:Ignore it if no other vehicles are present.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Stop and treat the intersection like a stop sign.,d:Slow down and proceed if clear.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a turn lane to turn left and there is oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.,d:Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left.
note: Before making a left turn, you should signal at least 100 feet before the turn so other drivers know your intentions. While waiting to turn, keep your wheels pointed straight until you actually begin turning so that if you are hit from behind, you are not pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: If an approaching vehicle fails to dim their high beams, where should you focus?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, briefly glance toward the right side of your lane and use the road edge or lane markings as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you maintain a safe path without being blinded by the other vehicle’s headlights.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Alerts drivers to school zones.,b:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to existing or possible hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain speed and stay in your lane.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing lights and/or a siren, you must pull as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: How can you reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road and then resume forward scanning.,b:Stare at the centerline of the road.,c:Turn on your high beams to counter glare.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide while continuing to scan ahead. Do not stare directly into the oncoming headlights or at the centerline, and do not turn on your high beams toward oncoming traffic, as that increases glare for everyone.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.,b:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.,c:Ensure your tires are properly inflated.,d:All of the above.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To help prevent hydroplaning, you should keep your tires in good condition with adequate tread depth, make sure they are properly inflated, and reduce your speed when roads are wet. Worn or underinflated tires and high speeds greatly increase the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What is the best way to ensure safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.,c:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.
note: Before backing, walk around and check behind your vehicle for children, pedestrians, or objects that may be in your blind spots. Once inside, use your mirrors and look over your shoulder while backing slowly. Relying only on mirrors is not enough, and simply honking does not ensure the area is clear.

question: Which practice is recommended on slippery surfaces like snow or ice?
options: a:Increase your following distance and drive more slowly.,b:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.,c:Pump your brakes repeatedly to prevent skidding.,d:All of the above.
note: On slippery surfaces like snow or ice, you should slow down and use a low gear before going down steep hills to help control your speed without overusing the brakes. Increase your following distance so you have more time to stop. Modern vehicles with ABS should use steady, firm braking rather than pumping the brakes; pumping is mainly for vehicles without ABS and is used only when stopping, not to prevent brakes from freezing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to stop in a travel lane to let a passenger out?
options: a:True — you may stop if necessary.,b:False — you must not stop in travel lanes to let out passengers.
note: You must not stop in an active travel lane just to pick up or drop off passengers. Stopping in a moving lane blocks traffic and greatly increases the risk of rear‑end collisions. Instead, continue to a legal parking spot, a designated passenger loading zone, or a safe area out of the flow of traffic before letting passengers in or out.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck (no gates or flashing lights), you should:
options: a:Turn your radio down and proceed at usual speed.,b:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.,c:Proceed without stopping if no lights are flashing.,d:Only continue once cleared by a flagger.
note: At a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you must treat it with extra caution. Slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross the tracks only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. A flagger is not required for you to proceed; you are responsible for checking that it is safe.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,b:Drive at a reduced speed until destination.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue.,d:Open a window and keep driving.
note: To avoid the dangers of drowsy driving, stop and rest or switch drivers. Short breaks and shared driving are safer than trying to push through fatigue.

question: What does a green arrow lane-use signal above a lane mean?
options: a:You must use this lane only to make a left turn.,b:The signal is about to change to a red X.,c:You may drive in that lane normally (lane is open).
note: A green arrow lane‑use signal above a lane means that lane is open for travel in the direction of the arrow. You may drive in that lane, following all other signs and markings. Lane‑use signals are used on roads where the direction or availability of lanes can change, and a green arrow indicates you are allowed to use that lane.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is driving at night?
options: a:Less dangerous because traffic is lighter.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous due to reduced visibility and increased chance of impaired or tired drivers.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous than daytime driving. Your visibility is reduced, it is harder to judge distances and speeds, and glare from headlights can affect your vision. In addition, there is a higher chance of encountering tired or impaired drivers. Because of these factors, you must use extra caution and adjust your speed and following distance at night.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:Whenever you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens and/or flashing lights. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by law enforcement.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass by crossing the lines.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:The right lane may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road if it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: If a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Yield.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Honk to let them know you’re there.
note: When a transit vehicle (such as a city bus) signals that it is pulling away from a stop, you should be prepared to yield so it can safely re-enter traffic. Slowing and allowing the bus back into the lane helps prevent collisions and keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what is the safe action?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.
note: Large trucks and buses often need extra space and may swing wide to complete right turns. Never try to squeeze between a large vehicle and the curb. Stay behind and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its turn before you make your right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you should:
options: a:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.,b:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,c:Signal only after passing.,d:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
note: On a two-lane road, pass only when it is legal and safe. After passing, signal and return to your lane only when you have enough space—typically when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror—without cutting them off.

question: Which statement about changing weather is true?
options: a:You should always maintain the same speed regardless of rain or fog.,b:A sudden change in weather requires you to adjust your driving.,c:Weather does not affect stopping distance.,d:Ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.
note: A sudden change in weather can quickly reduce visibility and traction. When rain, fog, snow, or wind conditions change, you must adjust your speed, increase following distance, and drive more cautiously so you have enough time and space to react safely.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road and you begin to hydroplane, gently ease your foot off the accelerator. Do not brake hard or turn suddenly, because that can cause a skid. As your tires regain traction, you can steer and slow down more normally.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Interior dome lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without creating extra glare.

question: When changing lanes you should not:
options: a:Use a turn signal to indicate your intention.,b:Look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.,d:Fail to check your side and rearview mirrors for approaching traffic.
note: When changing lanes, you must check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. The one thing you must never do is change lanes without checking your side and rearview mirrors for approaching traffic, because you may move into the path of another vehicle.

question: Before turning on the ignition you should:
options: a:Buckle your own safety belt and make sure passengers are belted.,b:Make sure your radio is off.,c:Check your engine oil level.,d:Close all windows.
note: Always fasten your seat belt before driving and ensure passengers are also buckled; it is illegal in New Mexico to drive unbelted.

question: Signs colored orange normally indicate:
options: a:Regulatory requirements.,b:School zone warnings.,c:Work zones.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn drivers about construction, maintenance, or utility work so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, you cannot pass safely unless:
options: a:You are able to clearly see the road ahead.,b:You can clearly see the road ahead and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle can reach the speed needed to pass safely.,d:All of the above.
note: You should only pass on a two‑lane, two‑way road when all safety conditions are met: you can clearly see enough clear road ahead, you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can accelerate and pass without forcing any driver to slow or swerve. If any of these conditions are missing, you must not pass.

question: For a driver aged 21 or older, what BAC is illegal to drive at or above?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even lower levels can impair driving, but 0.08% is the standard per se legal limit for DUI for adults.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what else should occupants do?
options: a:Disable the airbags for safety.,b:Sit as far forward as possible.,c:Seat belts are not necessary.,d:Always wear seat belts as well.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can protect you and reduce the risk of being thrown from the vehicle. Always wear your seat belt, even in vehicles equipped with airbags.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary.,b:Keep driving normally if other lanes are available.,c:Stop immediately in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. On a divided multilane highway, slow down, move safely to the side to create a clear path, and stop if needed until the emergency vehicle has passed. Do not stop in the middle of a lane if you can move out of the way safely.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, what should drivers do?
options: a:Maintain speed and stay in the lane.,b:Pull to the right-hand edge of the roadway and wait for it to pass.,c:Stop in the intersection until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, allowing it a clear path. Do not stop in an intersection; if you are in one, continue through and then pull over to the right as soon as it is safe.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
note: A dashed yellow line beside a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic next to the dashed line. Drivers next to the solid line must not cross it to pass, because it marks a higher-risk area where passing is unsafe from that side.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line indicates:
options: a:Vehicles in both directions may pass.,b:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
note: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, only vehicles next to the broken line may pass when it is safe. The solid line side must not cross the line to pass, because it indicates that passing from that side is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Only stop if a police officer is nearby.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the light is green unless turning on red is permitted and safe.,c:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present.,d:Continue because they have the right-of-way.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line and remain stopped until the light turns green. In many areas you may turn right on red after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, but only if there is no sign prohibiting it and the turn can be made safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.,c:You have the right-of-way because the vehicle to your right goes first.
note: At a four-way stop, if you and another driver arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other driver is on your left, you are on their right, so you proceed first after stopping and making sure it is safe.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that a ____ light is about to appear.
options: a:Steady green,b:Steady red,c:Flashing yellow,d:Flashing red
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should prepare to stop and only proceed if you are too close to the intersection to stop safely.

question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn to warn them.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk, even if they are crossing against the signal. Stop and let them cross safely before proceeding.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Are better drivers because they're more cautious.,d:Should drive only in familiar areas.
note: Alcohol reduces judgment, coordination, and reaction time, so drivers who have been drinking cannot safely control their bodies or their vehicles. Any amount of alcohol can impair driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who must you yield to?
options: a:Drivers who arrived after you.,b:Drivers who signal first.,c:Drivers who arrived before you.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. You must yield to any driver who reached the intersection before you, then take your turn when it is safe.

question: What's the key point about speed management in curves?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter and slow at the sharpest part.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
note: Before entering a curve, reduce your speed so you can stay in your lane and avoid skidding outward. Entering too fast makes it harder to control the vehicle through the curve.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:
options: a:You may proceed in any direction slowly.,b:You may turn only in the direction of the green arrow (after yielding as required).,c:You may go straight only.,d:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
note: A green arrow with a red light means you have a protected turn only in the direction of the arrow. You must yield to any traffic or pedestrians still in the intersection, but you may not go straight or turn in any other direction.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Come to an immediate complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should slow down, scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, or hazards, and continue only when it is safe.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what is the proper action?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,c:Speed up to get out of the way in the next block.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights and siren on, you must pull as far to the right as possible and stop, allowing it a clear path. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over to the right and stop.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to get attention while stopped in the lane.,b:Pull off the roadway and onto the shoulder or emergency area, then turn on your hazard flashers.,c:Get out and wave down passing cars.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, move completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder or an emergency area. Turn on your hazard flashers so other drivers can see you, and stay in the vehicle with your seat belt on if it is safe to do so. Walking along high‑speed roads or standing near moving traffic is very dangerous.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check blind spots?
options: a:When pulling toward or away from a curb or merging.,b:When turning left or right at an intersection.,c:Whenever you change lanes or merge into another lane of traffic.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. You must look over your shoulder to check these areas whenever you change lanes, merge, or move toward or away from a curb. This quick glance helps you spot vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians that might be hidden in your mirrors.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop even without a stop sign present.,b:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when children are nearby.
note: School crossing signs warn that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be ready to stop for anyone in or about to enter the crosswalk. You do not always have to stop unless a child is in the crosswalk, a crossing guard directs you to stop, or a traffic control device requires it.

question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?
options: a:Just before changing lanes.,b:After changing lanes.,c:Early enough (at least 100 feet in advance at lower speeds) before you change lanes to pass.
note: You must signal well before you change lanes so other drivers have time to see your signal and react. At speeds under 40 mph, signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning; at higher speeds, signal even earlier. Signaling only as you move, or after you move, does not give others enough warning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:All of the above.,d:Sound your horn before moving.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must signal your intention, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. This combination ensures you do not move into a space already occupied or about to be occupied by another vehicle. Sounding your horn is not normally required for lane changes.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Yellow and white,c:Yellow
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction and also mark edges of the roadway. When you see a yellow centerline, expect oncoming traffic on the other side.

question: Is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages inside a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Yes — if you are sitting in the back seat.,b:Yes — if you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.,c:No — it is illegal in most states to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public highway.
note: Open container laws in most U.S. states make it illegal to drink alcohol or have an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road, regardless of whether you are in the front or back seat or in the back of a pickup. Open containers must be in a trunk or other area not normally occupied by people.

question: At a red light that shows a green arrow for your direction, when may you proceed?
options: a:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:Only after the green arrow changes to a solid green.
note: A green arrow at a red light means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. If you are in the correct lane and the path is clear of vehicles, pedestrians, and other hazards, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow even though the main signal is red.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your right foot for both acceleration and braking.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Use whichever foot feels comfortable, even the left.,d:Use both feet simultaneously for better control.
note: You should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. Using only the right foot helps prevent accidentally pressing both pedals or confusing them, which can lead to loss of control or longer stopping distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate from a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Enter only after you have a safe gap in traffic and accelerate quickly to match traffic speed.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and then speed up.,c:Use the shoulder to reach traffic speed.
note: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you must yield to interstate traffic. Slow or stop if needed at the end of the ramp, wait until you see a safe gap, then accelerate quickly to match traffic speed as you merge. Never use the shoulder as a driving lane.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through the zone quickly.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Maintain your normal speed through the zone.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey all posted work zone signs, and be prepared to stop suddenly. Lanes may narrow, traffic may shift, and workers or equipment can be close to moving traffic, so extra caution and lower speeds are required.

question: Holding a driver's license is considered a:
options: a:Right that cannot be revoked.,b:Requirement you must carry at all times.,c:Permanent entitlement.,d:Privilege
note: A driver’s license is a privilege granted by the state, not a guaranteed right. It can be suspended or revoked if you violate traffic laws, drive unsafely, or fail to meet legal requirements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure to enter a gap in highway traffic?
options: a:Check behind you and to the sides, then watch the vehicle ahead before merging.,b:Speed up and expect other drivers to make room.,c:Rely only on vehicles behind the gap.
note: Before merging into highway traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots to the sides and behind you, signal, and make sure there is a large enough gap. Adjust your speed so you can smoothly enter the gap without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with blocked view from oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Rely on another driver to wave you through.,b:Accelerate quickly when the first lane clears.,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before completing the turn.
note: When turning left across multiple lanes, do not begin your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic. Never rely on another driver waving you through; you are responsible for making sure the way is clear and safe.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct first action?
options: a:Brake hard immediately and turn sharply.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to keep control, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, then move off the road to a safe place when you have the vehicle under control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:Any speed below the limit regardless of conditions.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for the conditions.,c:The posted maximum speed only.
note: You must always drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, even if that is below the posted speed limit. The posted limit is the maximum under ideal conditions, not a guaranteed safe speed in all situations.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, prescription or over-the-counter medications, and lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription medications, some over‑the‑counter medicines, and fatigue. All of these can slow your reactions, affect judgment, and reduce awareness, making driving unsafe.

question: True or false: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your chance of a crash.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only if using hands-free,d:Only when driving under 25 mph.
note: Using a cell phone while driving, whether talking or texting, significantly increases your risk of a crash because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind away from driving. Even hands‑free use can distract your attention from the road, so the statement that it does not significantly increase crash risk is false.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you expect?
options: a:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.,b:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,c:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
note: When driving past parked vehicles, you must anticipate that a door could open, a car could pull out, or a pedestrian could step into your lane without warning. Leave extra space from the parked cars and be ready to slow or stop if someone suddenly enters your path.

question: Like alcohol or drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:It has no effect on driving ability.,b:It improves attention.,c:It can impair your judgment and slow reaction time.
note: Drowsiness makes you less alert, slows your reaction time, and affects your judgment, much like alcohol or drugs. A drowsy driver may not notice hazards in time or may react too slowly to avoid a crash.

question: What is the only medically proven method to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Give your body time.,c:Exercise vigorously.,d:Drink coffee.
note: The only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration is to allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise might make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how quickly alcohol leaves your system or make you safe to drive.

question: When passing large vehicles you should be careful because:
options: a:They always signal before changing lanes.,b:They cannot be passed on the highway.,c:They have large blind spots and you should avoid driving beside them for long periods.,d:They always travel slower than traffic.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along the sides, rear, and sometimes in front of the vehicle. If you drive beside them for too long, the driver may not see you. Pass large vehicles promptly and safely, or drop back so you stay out of their blind spots.

question: How can you avoid loss of traction (hydroplaning) on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Drive with your parking lights on.,c:Slow down.,d:Apply the brakes firmly and suddenly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to prevent this is to slow down in wet conditions and make smooth, gradual steering and braking inputs. Good tire tread and proper inflation also help maintain traction.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn a child who is about to run into the street.,b:When passing a bicyclist.,c:While traveling through an intersection to hurry traffic.,d:To express frustration at another driver.
note: Use your horn only as a warning to help prevent a collision, such as when a child or pedestrian is about to enter the street and may not see you. Do not use the horn to express anger, to hurry other drivers, or unnecessarily around bicyclists or at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road, when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you provide?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Demand the other driver move over.,c:Allow at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle.
note: On narrow two-way roads, each driver must share the roadway so that both vehicles can pass safely. You must allow at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle, rather than forcing the other driver off the road or demanding they move.

question: When driving in rain, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights only.,b:Use parking lights only.,c:Use low beam headlights.,d:Use high beam headlights.
note: In rain, always use low beam headlights so you can see and be seen without causing glare. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or snow and actually reduce your ability to see. Parking lights or hazard lights alone are not sufficient or legal substitutes for headlights while driving.

question: Which effects can alcoholic beverages have on a driver?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking, and give a false sense of confidence.,b:They always improve coordination.,c:They have no impact on judgment.
note: Alcohol affects the brain and nervous system, slowing reaction time, impairing judgment and thinking, reducing coordination, and often giving a false sense of confidence. These effects greatly increase the risk of a crash, even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

question: If you are sharing the road with a motorcycle, what must you allow it?
options: a:Driving on the shoulder beside you.,b:Use of only half a lane.,c:Use of a full traffic lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like any other motor vehicle. Do not crowd them or share the lane side‑by‑side; give them the entire lane width so they have room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Keeping eye contact during a conversation with a passenger.,b:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.,c:Focusing only on the vehicle directly ahead.
