note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as daydreaming or looking away from the road at objects off the roadway. Safe drivers keep their attention on the road and continually scan ahead, to the sides, and in mirrors.

question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:It is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:It is a school bus.,c:It indicates a vehicle carrying hazardous materials.,d:It is an ambulance.
note: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle is the slow‑moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, such as farm machinery or horse‑drawn vehicles, so you should slow down and pass only when safe.

question: Which devices are commonly used on highways to direct drivers into the proper turning lanes?
options: a:Lane arrows and pavement markings indicating turning lanes.,b:Flashing red lights only.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: Highways commonly use lane arrows on signs and pavement markings to show which lanes are for turning or going straight. Drivers should follow these arrows and markings to be in the correct lane before reaching an intersection or exit.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams and, if equipped and legal, fog lights help you see the road more clearly.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing the street.,c:Continue ahead—the motorist has the right-of-way.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians within a crosswalk and wait until the crossing is clear before proceeding.

question: When a curb is painted which color, it usually indicates a loading zone or parking restriction?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Yellow
note: Painted curbs indicate parking rules. A yellow curb commonly marks a loading zone or an area where stopping or standing is restricted or time-limited. Always check nearby signs for specific rules.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Increase following distance later.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Reduce your speed.,d:Turn on interior lights.
note: When visibility drops, your first reaction should be to slow down. Reducing speed gives you more time to see and react to hazards. Then, as needed, use headlights and wipers and increase following distance.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up as he or she is passing you.,b:Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.,c:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.
note: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, the safest response is to stay calm and, when it is safe, move out of their way. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or speeding up, as these can escalate the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true about passing and signaling?
options: a:You only need to signal at any time.,b:Return to your lane before you can see the passed car in your rearview mirror.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check mirrors and blind spots.
note: Before passing, signal early—at least 100 feet before changing lanes in most areas—then check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:
options: a:More coordinated.,b:More intoxicated.,c:Less affected.,d:More sober.
note: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) goes up, alcohol has a stronger effect on your brain and body. Your judgment, coordination, and reaction time get worse, so you become more impaired and more intoxicated, not more coordinated or more sober.

question: Emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights:
options: a:Do not need to be given any special consideration.,b:May not use loudspeakers for instructions.,c:May be passed quickly by other drivers.,d:Have the right-of-way; you must yield and follow any instructions given by their loudspeaker.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over and stop, and follow any instructions given over a loudspeaker. Do not try to pass or block the vehicle.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way when they are in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,b:Anyone in a marked or unmarked crosswalk or intersection.,c:Only pedestrians crossing at intersections with signals.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. An unmarked crosswalk is the extension of the sidewalk across the intersection, even if there are no painted lines. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: What must you do when you encounter lowered gates and flashing lights at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they are raised and the tracks are clear.,b:Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,c:Slowly drive under the gate if no train is visible.
note: Lowered gates and flashing lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop well before the gate, never drive around or under it, and wait until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and you can clearly see that the tracks are safe and clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto interstate traffic, after checking for a gap and signaling, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the lane to be completely clear before merging.,b:Merge carefully into the gap when safe.,c:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and then merge into a suitable gap when it is safe. Do not stop and wait for the lane to be empty, and do not assume other drivers must yield to you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you drive on the right shoulder of the road?
options: a:When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.,b:When the car in front of you is turning.,c:Only when told to do so by an official.
note: You may only drive on the shoulder when directed by an official; do not use shoulders to pass other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when:
options: a:You are on a hill or curve with limited visibility.,b:There is a solid line next to your lane indicating no passing.,c:You are in a lane next to a broken line and it is safe to do so.,d:You cannot see ahead clearly.
note: You may pass when the line next to your lane is broken and the way ahead is clear; never pass where lines indicate you may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?
options: a:On a straight roadway with clear view for 500 feet.,b:Where a sign specifically allows U-turns.,c:On or near any curve or hill where you cannot be seen by others.,d:In a parking lot.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where oncoming traffic cannot see you in time to avoid a collision.

question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane (skid on water), should you quickly apply the brakes? True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, you should not brake suddenly. Sudden braking can cause a complete loss of control. Instead, ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and allow the vehicle to slow down gradually until the tires regain traction.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery?
options: a:After several hours of steady rain.,b:Just after it begins to rain.,c:One to two hours after rain starts.
note: Roads are especially slick at the start of rainfall because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with water, producing a greasy film.

question: When driving on major highways, you should:
options: a:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead at all times.,b:Drive at a constant speed regardless of conditions.,c:Avoid changing lanes even if needed.,d:Stay alert and keep scanning the road for hazards.
note: On highways you must stay alert and continuously scan ahead, to the sides, and in your mirrors. Moving your eyes helps you spot hazards early, avoid highway hypnosis, and react in time to changing traffic or road conditions.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information and guidance for drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings are an important part of the traffic control system. They guide lane use, show where passing is allowed, indicate turn lanes, mark crosswalks, and warn of changes ahead. Drivers must understand and follow these markings to stay in the correct lane and drive safely.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:As a signal to speed up.,b:As a yield sign—slow but do not stop.,c:As a stop sign—come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before entering the intersection, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median, what should drivers on your side do?
options: a:Stop until the bus's stop arm is lifted even on a divided highway.,b:Continue driving; you do not need to stop when you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a median.,c:Stop until the bus begins moving.
note: On a divided highway with a physical median or barrier, drivers traveling on the opposite side from a stopped school bus are generally not required to stop. However, you should stay alert, obey the speed limit, and be prepared for children who may be near the roadway. If there is no physical median or the road is not truly divided, you must stop for the bus.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Use high beams at all times to see better.,c:Keep instrument lighting bright to be seen by others.
note: At night you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate. This ensures you have enough time to see and react to hazards in the roadway before you reach them.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Limit driving to weekdays.,c:Drive slowly at all times.,d:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a properly adjusted seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, reduce impact with the interior, and help you stay in control of the vehicle during emergency maneuvers.

question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Treat it like a red light.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,d:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic if they are in or entering the intersection.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light as you approach an intersection?
options: a:Stop completely before entering,b:Slow down and proceed with caution after checking for cross traffic.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should slow down, look carefully for pedestrians and cross traffic, and proceed only if the way is clear. It is a warning to use extra caution, not a requirement to stop and wait for a green light.

question: If a vehicle with high beams approaches and does not dim them, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the centerline of the road.,c:Either side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, briefly glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge of the road or lane line as a guide. This reduces glare in your eyes while still allowing you to see the roadway and stay in your lane.

question: Which steps help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:Allowing extra travel time.
note: To reduce road rage and aggressive driving, you should use several strategies together: obey posted speed limits so you are not rushing or tailgating, use proper turn signals so others can anticipate your actions, and allow extra travel time so you are less likely to become impatient or frustrated in traffic.

question: When you see a school crossing (pentagonal) sign, what should you do?
options: a:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop whether or not a stop sign is present.,c:Sound your horn to warn nearby children.
note: A pentagonal school sign warns that you are near a school or school crossing. You should slow down, watch carefully for children who may enter the road unexpectedly, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,c:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing despite the flagger's instructions.
note: In construction zones, flaggers have the legal authority to direct traffic. You must obey their signals and instructions, even if they differ from traffic lights or signs, because they are managing traffic around hazards and workers.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is true?
options: a:You must stay within your lane, but may change lanes when it is safe.,b:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,c:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes when it is safe, but you are still required to stay within your lane except when making a safe lane change.

question: Where are stop lines painted across lanes?
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and before crosswalks. They show you where to stop your vehicle so you do not block the crosswalk or enter the intersection before it is safe or legal.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes mean?
options: a:You may only change lanes from the left lane.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
note: A single broken white line means traffic in both lanes is moving in the same direction and you may cross the line to change lanes or pass when it is safe. Always check mirrors and blind spots and ensure you have enough space before moving.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit.,b:Stop and back up on the freeway.,c:Make a U-turn through the median.,d:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, keep going to the next exit, then safely leave the freeway and turn around as needed. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the freeway or median, because high speeds and limited reaction time make those maneuvers extremely dangerous.

question: On the highway, regularly looking far ahead of your vehicle helps you to:
options: a:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Helps you keep up with traffic.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.,d:Makes lane changes unnecessary.
note: Looking far ahead on the highway lets you see problems early, such as slowing traffic, lane closures, or debris. This gives you more time to react smoothly, reducing sudden braking or swerving and helping traffic flow more safely.

question: If a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload and its lights are flashing, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Slow and pass cautiously on the right.,c:Pass immediately on the left if no children are seen.,d:Proceed at reduced speed without stopping.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. On undivided roads, drivers in both directions must stop; on divided highways, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop, unless state law says otherwise.

question: Ramps and bridges often freeze before roadways do.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Ramps and bridges freeze before regular roadways because cold air surrounds them from above and below, causing the surface temperature to drop faster. In freezing or near-freezing weather, approach bridges, overpasses, and ramps with extra caution and reduce speed.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:On the side with the lightest traffic.,b:On the same side as traffic flow.,c:On the side facing oncoming traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This allows them to see approaching vehicles and move out of the way if needed, and it also makes them more visible to drivers.

question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or are crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Will drive no differently than when thinking clearly.,b:Should take time to calm down and focus before driving.,c:Can drive faster because senses are heightened.,d:Continue driving and hope feelings pass.
note: Emotions like anger, fear, or crying can distract you, slow your reactions, and cause poor decisions. You should wait until you have calmed down and can focus fully on driving before getting behind the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic while your signal is green, what should you do?
options: a:Don't enter until you can get completely across.,b:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,c:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.
note: A green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. You must not enter unless there is enough space to clear it completely. Entering and stopping in the intersection can block cross traffic and is illegal in many states.

question: What does a \No passing zone\" sign tell drivers?"
options: a:It is not safe or legal to pass in the indicated area.,b:To maintain a steady speed.,c:To speed up slightly to pass other vehicles.,d:That passing is permitted during daylight only.
note: A "No Passing Zone" sign means you must not pass other vehicles in that area. These zones are placed where passing would be unsafe, such as on hills, curves, or where visibility is limited.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a motorcycle in good weather.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view and when visibility or road conditions are poor.
note: You should leave more space when following large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, on slippery roads, in heavy traffic, or when being tailgated. Extra distance gives you more time to react and stop safely.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Because they don't follow traffic rules on purpose.,b:Because children are smaller and less predictable.,c:Because they can ride faster than adults.
note: Children on bicycles are smaller, harder to see, and often unpredictable because they may not fully understand traffic rules. Give them extra space and slow down, especially near schools, neighborhoods, and parks.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Continue at normal speed without looking for hazards.,d:Yield only to vehicles on your left.
note: A flashing yellow light is a warning signal. You are not required to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is a common risk of driving on worn or bald tires?
options: a:They are more likely to hydroplane.,b:They improve cornering control.,c:They reduce stopping distance.
note: Worn or bald tires have very little tread, so they cannot channel water away effectively. This makes the vehicle much more likely to hydroplane, reduces traction, and increases stopping distance, especially on wet roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a multi-lane street in your direction of travel, where should you enter?
options: a:Into the lane closest to the lane you came from.,b:Always into the far left lane.,c:Into the lane marked by a painted arrow only.
note: When you turn onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you were in before the turn. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles turning from the opposite direction.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:Proceed through the intersection if the road is clear (or turn if not prohibited),c:Always slow and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if turning is not prohibited, but only when the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any oncoming traffic when turning left.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Relax, concentrate on driving, and not take other drivers' actions personally.,b:Drive above posted speeds to keep traffic moving.,c:Tailgate slow drivers to prompt them to speed up.,d:Use your horn frequently to express displeasure.
note: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm, focus on the road, and do not take other drivers’ mistakes or rude actions personally. Allow extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and avoid tailgating, honking in anger, or making gestures.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, how should you respond?
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and drive through the smoke.,b:Reduce speed and be prepared to pull over and stop in a safe place if you cannot see ahead.,c:Turn on high-beam headlights and continue.
note: When you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down, move to the right as far as safely possible, and be prepared to stop completely off the roadway if you cannot see. Use low‑beam headlights and, if stopped, your hazard flashers so others can see you. Do not drive blindly into smoke where visibility is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do even if the light is green?
options: a:Turn left and find another route immediately.,b:Follow other vehicles into the intersection and wait there.,c:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space on the other side for your vehicle to clear it completely. Even with a green light, entering when traffic is stopped ahead can leave you blocking the intersection, which is unsafe and can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:At railroad crossings.,b:On hills and curves.,c:At intersections.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing is prohibited in several locations because sight distance and conflict risk are high. You must not pass at railroad crossings, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or at intersections unless specifically allowed. Always obey pavement markings and signs that indicate no passing zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever legal to block an intersection?
options: a:Yes,b:Only during rush hour.,c:No — you must not enter unless you can clear the intersection.
note: You may not legally block an intersection. Only enter when you are sure you can drive all the way through without stopping. Even with a green light, if traffic ahead is stopped and there is not enough room for your vehicle on the far side, you must wait behind the stop line.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake hard immediately.,d:Ease off the pedals and steer in the direction of the skid.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator and brakes, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (often described as steering in the direction of the skid). Sudden hard braking or jerking the wheel can make the skid worse and cause you to lose control.

question: If a transit (bus) signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping, what is required of you?
options: a:Move to the left lane.,b:Honk to let them know you're there.,c:Yield to the transit vehicle.
note: When a bus signals that it is pulling away from a stop, you must allow it to merge back into traffic when it is safe. Yielding gives the bus space and time to re-enter the lane smoothly and protects boarding or exiting passengers.

question: How can sudden wind gusts affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They only cause visibility problems.,b:They only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:They can cause problems for all vehicles
note: Strong or sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, making it harder to stay in your lane. They can be especially dangerous when passing large trucks or on bridges and open stretches, and they may also blow dust or debris that reduces visibility.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:It causes pollution only.,b:It can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning.,c:It can cause a loss of hearing.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide enter the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can quickly cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: Which of these is NOT a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Reaction distance.,b:Steering ability.,c:Braking distance.
note: Total stopping distance is made up of perception distance (seeing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (the distance the vehicle travels while slowing to a stop). Steering ability does not directly change how far it takes to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing an intersection without traffic lights, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,b:Whoever started moving last must yield.,c:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian.
note: When turning at an intersection without traffic lights, you must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the street you are turning into. Pedestrians in the crosswalk or crossing at the intersection have the right-of-way, whether or not the crosswalk is painted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When considering right-of-way, what is the safest assumption for a driver?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Rely solely on traffic signals to determine right-of-way.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,d:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: You can never safely assume that other drivers will follow right‑of‑way rules, even when you are legally entitled to go. Defensive drivers always stay ready to yield if it will prevent a collision, because avoiding a crash is more important than insisting on your legal right-of-way.

question: What is the typical shape and color of temporary construction/work zone signs?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black markings.,b:Round with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary construction and work zone signs are usually orange with black letters or symbols and are often diamond-shaped, though some may be rectangular. The orange color alerts drivers to changing road conditions and the need to slow down and use extra caution.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Pass on the right regardless of conditions.,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist then pass quickly.,c:Drive into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,d:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as safely possible, ideally at least several feet or as required by state law. Bicyclists are vulnerable and may need to swerve to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors, so extra space and reduced speed help prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Turn either right or left because the road is blocked ahead.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Stop only if other vehicles are present.,d:Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other road users, and proceed only when it is safe and the intersection is clear.

question: Excessive speed most often leads to what?
options: a:High-risk decision-making and increased crash risk.,b:No change in crash likelihood.,c:Improved ability to react to hazards.
note: Driving at excessive speed reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards, increases stopping distance, and makes crashes more likely and more severe. Higher speeds often lead to poor decisions, such as late braking or unsafe lane changes, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,b:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,c:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to slow or stop. If you brake suddenly in front of them, the driver may not be able to stop in time, increasing the risk of a rear‑end collision. Always avoid cutting closely in front of large vehicles and leave extra space when changing lanes.

question: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires:
options: a:Provide the same traction as on asphalt.,b:Grip the road better than on pavement.,c:Do not have as much traction as on pavement,d:Allow you to stop more quickly.
note: On gravel or dirt, the loose surface reduces how well your tires can grip the road. Because traction is lower than on pavement, it takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid, especially when braking or turning suddenly. Slow down and increase your following distance on these surfaces.

question: In very heavy fog you should slow down and:
options: a:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,b:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.,c:Turn on parking lights only.,d:Turn on your emergency flashers.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it even harder to see. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road and other vehicles more clearly. Slow down, increase following distance, and be prepared to stop if visibility becomes too poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while a traffic light is green, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer's directions even if they conflict with the traffic signal.,b:Obey the traffic signal instead of the officer.,c:Follow the car in front of you as a guide.,d:Ignore the officer if the light is green.
note: A police officer’s directions override traffic signals, signs, and road markings. If an officer signals you to stop, you must do so even if the traffic light is green. Follow the officer’s instructions carefully and safely, using your signals and checking traffic as you slow and stop.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To turn left into a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,c:To pass another car in traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you may not cross them to pass another vehicle. However, you may cross them when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when making a legal U‑turn where it is specifically permitted. Always check for oncoming traffic and yield as required before turning.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as your speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:Your tires become less effective at removing water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.,b:Water has no effect on modern tires.,c:Deep water is safer than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on a wet road, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. When they can’t clear the water fast enough, the tires ride up on a thin film of water instead of gripping the pavement, which greatly increases the risk of hydroplaning.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should:
options: a:Be hidden under your clothing.,b:Be left loose for comfort.,c:Be buckled snugly across your hip bones and low on your pelvis (not across your stomach).,d:Wrap around your neck.
note: A lap belt should fit snugly across the hips and low on the pelvis, not across the soft abdomen, to spread crash forces over the stronger hip bones. The shoulder belt should cross the center of the chest and shoulder, away from the neck, and never be worn under the arm or behind the back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:One driver may proceed without stopping.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the right may proceed first when it is safe, then the other driver goes.

question: What are the colors of signs that show distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Red with white letters.,d:Blue with white letters.
note: Freeway guide and exit signs that show directions and distances are green with white letters or symbols. These signs help you identify routes, exits, and distances to upcoming destinations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:By using the shoulder of the highway.,b:In a curve or on a hill.,c:If the yellow line next to your lane is broken and the passing lane is clear ahead.
note: You may pass only when the line next to your lane is broken and you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely. A solid yellow line on your side means no passing from your lane, but if the solid line is on the other side and your side has a broken yellow line, you may pass when it is safe and legal. Never pass on hills, curves, or by driving on the shoulder.

question: Which action best helps you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Deciding before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply telling others you won't drive after drinking if offered a drink.,c:Calling a taxi only after you've been drinking.
note: Deciding before you drink that you will not drive is the safest choice because alcohol quickly impairs judgment and self-control. Once you have been drinking, you are more likely to underestimate your level of impairment and overestimate your ability to drive safely. Planning ahead—such as arranging a sober driver or alternate transportation—prevents you from making a risky decision after you are impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:You see a police car.,b:You are entering a highway where there are other cars.,c:When conditions (weather, road, visibility) make driving less than perfect.,d:Only when other drivers are going slower than the limit.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions, not a guaranteed safe speed at all times. You must slow down below the limit when rain, snow, ice, fog, heavy traffic, poor road surfaces, or limited visibility make normal speeds unsafe. Driving at a speed that is too fast for conditions can be illegal even if you are below the posted limit.

question: What does a red arrow pointing right mean on a traffic signal?
options: a:You may turn after coming to a complete stop.,b:You may turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:You must not turn in that direction until the arrow turns green or a green light allows the turn.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow while it is red. You must remain stopped until the signal changes to a green arrow or a green light that permits the turn. Unlike a solid red light, where right turns on red may be allowed after stopping (unless prohibited), a red arrow specifically prohibits turning in that direction.

question: If another vehicle cuts closely in front of you, what should you do first?
options: a:Swerve into the next lane.,b:Take your foot off the accelerator to increase the following distance.,c:Honk and brake hard immediately.
note: When another vehicle cuts closely in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator to increase your following distance. This creates more space and time to react without sudden braking or swerving, which could cause a rear-end collision or loss of control. Only brake more firmly if needed to avoid a collision, and avoid swerving into another lane unless you are sure it is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Refuse to allow other cars to pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to bunch up and make risky passing maneuvers. If vehicles are stacking up behind you and it is safe to do so, you should pull off to the right side of the road or into a turnout area and let them pass. Many states specifically require slow-moving drivers on two-lane roads to use turnouts when several vehicles are lined up behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a driver behind you signals to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to prevent the pass.,b:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the pass.,c:Maintain your speed so they pass quickly.
note: When another driver signals to pass, you should help them do it safely. Gently reduce your speed to create more space in front of your vehicle so they have a longer, safer passing area and can move back into the lane without cutting closely in front of you.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on a long trip?
options: a:Turning up the car radio.,b:Slowing down while continuing to drive.,c:Stop at regular intervals for rest and stretching.
note: The only reliable way to prevent drowsiness on a long trip is to rest. Plan to stop at regular intervals to get out, walk, stretch, and, if needed, take a short nap. Tricks like turning up the radio or just slowing down do not keep you alert and can give a false sense of safety.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Drink coffee and continue driving.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Stop to rest or switch drivers.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop in a safe place to rest or switch drivers—driving while tired slows reactions and increases crash risk.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your low beam headlights:
options: a:False,b:Only when the fog is dense,c:True,d:Only on highways
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and vehicles ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view at an intersection is blocked, what's the correct approach?
options: a:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Stop
note: If your view at an intersection is blocked, you must first stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or edge of the intersection. Then move forward slowly, inching out until you can clearly see cross traffic in both directions before you proceed.

question: Which of these does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:None of the above.,b:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,c:Your judgement of speed and distance is distorted.,d:You are less alert.
note: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time, makes you less alert, and distorts your judgment of speed and distance. Because all of the listed effects do occur after drinking, the correct choice is that none of them are exceptions.

question: If you're angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music to avoid thinking about the argument.,b:Drive on the interstate to cool off.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before getting behind the wheel.
note: Strong emotions like anger can distract you, reduce your judgment, and make you more likely to take risks. It is safest to wait and calm down before driving so you can focus fully on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Yield to other cars.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Go.,d:Speed up to beat the red.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop, unless you are so close to the intersection that stopping suddenly would be unsafe.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Certain allergy medicines,b:Marijuana,c:Cold remedies,d:All of the above
note: Many drugs, including marijuana and some allergy or cold medicines, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or less alert. Any drug that affects your mind or body can impair driving, so always check labels and warnings before you drive.

question: If you have a tire blowout, which steps are recommended?
options: a:Apply the brakes immediately and firmly.,b:Keep accelerating to reach a safe area.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: If you have a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking; once you have control and your speed has dropped, gently brake as needed and steer to a safe place off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: When approaching a stop sign that has no marked crosswalk, drivers must stop before entering the intersection.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if a crosswalk exists.,d:Only at night.
note: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection so you can see cross traffic and yield properly.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Interior dome lights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:High beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, you should use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can make it harder to see, and parking lights or interior lights do not improve your view of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Toward the left.,b:Keep them straight ahead.,c:Toward the right (into the curb).
note: When parking facing downhill on a street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will rest against the curb and the car will roll away from moving traffic.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Turn and look out your back window.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, check your rearview mirror regularly. This helps you see vehicles that may be following too closely, preparing to pass, or approaching quickly so you can adjust your driving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, you should:
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible to clear the intersection.,b:Ignore pedestrian crossings until the light cycles again.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,d:Back up slowly to allow others to move.
note: A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles still in the intersection that entered on a previous signal.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams at night, what is the safest action?
options: a:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.,b:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look straight ahead in your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the glare can temporarily blind you. To protect your night vision, avoid looking directly at the headlights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to keep track of the road and the oncoming vehicle. This reduces glare while still allowing you to stay safely in your lane.

question: What should you avoid doing when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Following the posted detour signs.,b:Passing with extra caution.,c:Slowing down to stare at the scene (rubbernecking).
note: Slowing down just to stare at road work, crashes, or workers—called rubbernecking—is dangerous and often illegal. It distracts you from the road, increases the chance of rear-end collisions, and contributes to traffic jams. In construction zones you should slow to the posted work-zone speed, follow detours and signs, and pass carefully while staying focused on the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass in which situations?
options: a:When school bus lights are flashing.,b:On a hill or curve.,c:All of the above.,d:When approaching an intersection.
note: You must not pass when a school bus has flashing red lights, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or when approaching or driving through an intersection. These situations all limit visibility or involve vulnerable road users, making passing unsafe and often illegal. If any of these conditions exist, stay in your lane and wait until it is clearly safe and legal to pass.

question: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be no farther than what distance from the curb?
options: a:Six inches.,b:18 inches.,c:14 inches.,d:10 inches.
note: In most U.S. jurisdictions, when you parallel park your vehicle must be within about 18 inches of the curb. Parking too far from the curb can block traffic and create a hazard for cyclists and other vehicles. After parking, check that your wheels are reasonably close and parallel to the curb so your vehicle is safely out of the traffic lane.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train but continue if nothing is visible.,b:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly.,c:Stop and look for a train; remain at least 15 feet from the nearest rail if warning devices are active.
note: Flashing lights, gates, or bells at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop and wait, not try to beat the train. Stop no closer than about 15 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until the warning devices stop operating and you are sure all tracks are clear before crossing.

question: Must you yield the right-of-way to a disabled pedestrian using a cane, guide dog, or other device?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks, and this protection fully includes disabled pedestrians using white canes, guide dogs, wheelchairs, or other assistive devices. These pedestrians may need more time and space to cross, so slow down early and be prepared to stop.

question: What is the correct method for backing a vehicle safely?
options: a:Open your door to look behind you.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors and sensors.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.
note: To back safely, place your right arm over the seat, turn your head and upper body, and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Mirrors and sensors are helpful but can miss small children, pets, or low objects, so you should never rely on them alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:Only during daytime.,b:False,c:Only when other vehicles are nearby.,d:True
note: You must signal any time you move your vehicle laterally on the roadway, including when pulling away from a curb. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know you are about to re-enter traffic so they can adjust their speed or position safely.

question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid applying the brakes.,c:Drive at a constant speed to gain traction.,d:Turn sharply to regain control.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. If this occurs, ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, which can cause a skid; steer gently in the direction you want to go.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, you should:
options: a:Back up slowly while looking only in your mirrors.,b:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,c:Get out of the vehicle and walk to the rear to be sure the way is clear.,d:Rev the engine to warn the children.
note: Children can be hard to see directly behind a vehicle, especially in blind zones. Before backing out of a driveway where children are nearby, get out and walk behind the vehicle to make sure the area is clear, then back up slowly while continuing to check around you.

question: At night, which is the hardest to see?
options: a:Streetlights.,b:Other motorists.,c:Pedestrians.,d:Road signs.
note: Pedestrians are much less visible at night than illuminated objects like streetlights, vehicle headlights, or reflective road signs. Because they are often wearing dark clothing and are not lit, you must scan carefully and reduce speed in areas where people may be walking.

question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:Only when you see a toll booth.,b:After you have moved into the exit lane.,c:On the main road just before the exit lane.
note: On freeways and highways, you should maintain the normal traffic speed on the main roadway, signal and move into the exit lane when it is safe, and then slow down to the posted exit or ramp speed after you are in the exit lane. Slowing on the main travel lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: A pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,c:Flash your lights.
note: When a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Drivers are required to yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians in crosswalks and should never try to speed up to pass in front of them or use lights or horn to pressure them. Always allow pedestrians to cross safely.

question: Is it lawful to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True — it is allowed if both fit.,b:False — you must not share a lane with a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. They need the entire lane width to maneuver, avoid hazards, and maintain a safe space cushion. Do not drive side‑by‑side with a motorcycle in the same lane; instead, follow at a safe distance or pass in an adjacent lane when it is legal and safe.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes if safe to do so.,b:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.,c:Letting go of the steering wheel.
note: If you are about to be struck from the rear, keep both hands on the steering wheel so you can maintain control of the vehicle. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and your back against the seat to reduce whiplash, and be ready to apply the brakes if it is safe so you are not pushed into another vehicle. Never let go of the steering wheel in this situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:At the rearview mirror.,b:Your right side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This shoulder check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles hidden beside you.

question: A curb painted which color indicates only short parking stops are permitted?
options: a:White.,b:Blue.,c:Yellow.
note: Curb colors indicate different parking rules. A yellow curb typically means you may stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight, which is considered a short stop. White curbs usually allow passenger loading or unloading for a limited time, but yellow is the standard color used to restrict parking to short loading stops.

question: To cross a railroad track safely you should:
options: a:Listen and look both ways for trains, and only proceed when it is safe.,b:Look both ways only when warning lights are flashing.,c:Cross quickly if a train is approaching.,d:Never stop if no gate is present.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be ready to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely. Always obey lights, gates, and other warning devices.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Pass with caution when safe.,b:Do not pass from your lane.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass other vehicles from your lane. It marks a no-passing zone because of limited visibility or other hazards. You may still turn left across it when safe, unless signs say otherwise, but you cannot use the opposing lane to pass.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving tend to:
options: a:Be exempt from distracted driving laws.,b:Make no driving errors.,c:Have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.,d:Drive more carefully because they are alert.
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and diverts your attention from the road. This makes it harder to maintain steady lane position and full control of the vehicle, increasing the risk of drifting, delayed reactions, and crashes.

question: Which of the following helps prevent crashes by informing others of your intentions?
options: a:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using horn when needed.,b:Ignore other drivers.,c:Drive only on side streets and avoid main roads.
note: Using turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when needed lets other road users know what you plan to do, which helps them react safely and reduces the chance of a crash.

question: What does a green arrow signal displayed for a turn mean?
options: a:It only applies on one-way streets.,b:You may proceed only if accompanied by a circular green light.,c:Traffic in the indicated lane may proceed to turn in the direction shown; it has the same authority as a circular green for that movement, but you must still yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. Oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing a red must yield to you, but you must still proceed carefully and be prepared to yield to anyone still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you make a right turn on red?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and if no sign prohibits it and it is safe.,b:Before coming to a complete stop.,c:If pedestrians have not yet crossed the crosswalk.
note: You may turn right on a solid red after a full stop if the turn is permitted and safe; yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: Which action most commonly blocks smooth traffic flow?
options: a:Driving at the posted speed limit.,b:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,d:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or roadside incident (rubbernecking) disrupts traffic flow, causes sudden braking, and can lead to more collisions. Focus on the road and keep a safe, steady speed.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.,c:Turning your head to look over your shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder to check the blind spot where another vehicle may be hidden.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn continuously.,b:Shift to neutral, steer to a safe place, then turn off the ignition without locking the steering and brake to a stop.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep calm, shift to neutral to disconnect the engine from the wheels, and steer to a safe place. Once you are in control and out of traffic, turn off the ignition without removing the key so the steering does not lock, then brake to a stop and secure the vehicle.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Because the speed limit increases at night.,b:Because there are fewer cars on the road at night.,c:Because distance and speed are harder to judge in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards and to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving. Your headlights limit how much of the road you can see, so you must slow down and increase following distance to compensate.

question: Is it ever permissible to drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:If no train is visible.,b:When the lights have stopped flashing.,c:When the train has passed.,d:Under no circumstances.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad gates, even if you do not see a train or believe it has already passed. Warning devices can activate before a second train arrives, and trains can be closer or faster than they appear. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and signals stop before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a traffic signal that is not operating, you must:
options: a:Drive quickly through to avoid congestion.,b:Come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection (treat as all-way stop).,c:Only stop if a police officer is present.,d:Proceed without stopping if the way is clear.
note: When a traffic signal is completely dark or not operating, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, then proceed only after yielding the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians who arrived first or are already in the intersection.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Adjust the rearview mirror frequently.,b:Honk right before changing lanes.,c:Quickly turn your head to check the blind spot in the direction you plan to move.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots, while also using your mirrors and signal. Do not rely only on mirrors or the horn to detect vehicles beside you.

question: Which substances can impair your driving and possibly result in a DUII?
options: a:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,b:All of the above.,c:Beer,d:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or some prescription medicines.
note: Driving can be impaired by any substance that affects your judgment, reaction time, or coordination. This includes alcohol such as beer, controlled substances (illegal drugs and some prescription medicines), and inhalants like glue or paint. If any of these impair your driving, you can be arrested for DUII.

question: What message is displayed on a red, octagonal sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:One-way.,c:Stop.
note: A red, octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the left and stop in the intersection.,b:Continue through the intersection,c:Stop immediately in the intersection and remain there.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way. If you are already in an intersection, continue through to clear the intersection first, then pull to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the requirements for interstate driving?
options: a:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Both of the above.
note: Interstate driving involves higher speeds and heavier, faster‑moving traffic. You must be able to safely handle increased speeds and also remain constantly alert to changing traffic, signs, and road conditions to drive safely on interstates.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,c:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
note: Drivers must yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks at all times, regardless of whether the pedestrian signals or is using a phone. You must slow or stop when necessary to allow pedestrians to cross safely.

question: When should you allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped?
options: a:At a stop sign regardless of slope.,b:When in the center lane of a multi-lane road.,c:When stopped on an incline (uphill).
note: When stopped uphill, leave extra space between you and the vehicle ahead. If the front vehicle rolls back when starting, the larger space cushion helps prevent a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an interstate via an exit ramp, when should you reduce speed?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: On freeways, stay at highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Once in the deceleration lane, reduce speed to the posted exit or advisory speed so you do not slow mainline traffic.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, how should you proceed?
options: a:Prepare to yield to any train and do not cross until you can clear the tracks completely.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks regardless of conditions.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and quickly.
note: At an unsignaled railroad crossing, slow, look, and listen for trains and be ready to stop. Never enter the tracks unless you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space beyond the tracks for your entire vehicle to clear them completely.

question: Changing lanes should be done:
options: a:Without signaling if the lane is clear.,b:Only when other vehicles are in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.,d:Quickly and often to keep traffic moving.
note: Change lanes only when necessary and safe. Signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, then move over gradually and smoothly without sudden swerves.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks if moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never stop on railroad tracks, even in heavy traffic. Do not enter the crossing unless there is enough room on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure when changing lanes?
options: a:Check the side mirror and glance over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down dramatically before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot. If the lane is clear, signal and change lanes smoothly without slowing abruptly.

question: How is 'distracted driving' best defined?
options: a:Any activity that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Something that usually improves driving performance.,c:Only activities that involve using a phone.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. This includes phone use, eating, adjusting controls, or interacting with passengers, and it greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must drivers yield?
options: a:Pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic, pedestrians in the crosswalk, and any vehicles already in the intersection. Do not start your turn until it is safe and all of these road users have cleared your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to warn drivers.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. If you are rear-ended while your wheels are turned left, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic. Only turn the wheels as you actually begin the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Always speed up to prevent merging.,c:Merge into another lane if possible or slow to create a gap.
note: On freeways, help entering vehicles merge safely by moving to another lane if it is safe, or by adjusting your speed to create a safe gap. Do not speed up to block them or hold a position that forces them to stop at the end of the ramp.

question: When making a left turn, must you yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if the bicyclist is in a bike lane.,d:Only at night.
note: Bicyclists are treated as vehicles. When you turn left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicycles approaching from the opposite direction, just as you would yield to oncoming cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals are not working, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Hand signals.,c:Sound your horn.
note: If your electrical turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show when you are turning or stopping so other road users can anticipate your actions.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brakes.,b:Hold down the brake pedal continuously.,c:Firmly pump your brakes to maintain steering control.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use firm, repeated pumping of the brakes in an emergency stop. This helps prevent the wheels from locking so you can maintain steering control while slowing quickly.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what are they signaling?
options: a:Turn right.,b:Come to a stop.,c:Turn left.,d:Slow down.
note: Standard hand signals: left arm straight out = left turn, left arm bent upward = right turn, and left arm bent downward = slow or stop. A left arm and hand extended upward means the driver intends to turn right.

question: When crossing a sidewalk from a driveway or alley, what should a driver do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.
note: When exiting a driveway, alley, or parking lot across a sidewalk, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and any traffic on the sidewalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way; do not expect them to yield to you.

question: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used to indicate:
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:No passing zones.,d:Construction zones.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are reserved for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: If an emergency vehicle with lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Drive with your flashers on and continue.,c:Speed up and exit the street.
note: On any roadway, including a one-way street, you must yield to approaching emergency vehicles using lights or siren. Move safely and promptly toward the nearest edge or curb of the roadway—right or left on a one-way street—and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck, what precaution should you take at railroad crossings?
options: a:Decrease your following distance so you can get around them quickly.,b:Pass them on the right.,c:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
note: School buses and many tank trucks carrying hazardous or flammable materials are required to stop at all railroad crossings, even if signals are not active. When following these vehicles, slow down and be ready to stop as they approach the tracks.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are making quick and sudden stops.,b:They are weaving between lanes.,c:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.
note: A common sign of an impaired or drunk driver is weaving or drifting between lanes. Other warning signs include driving much too slowly, making sudden or erratic stops, and inconsistent speed or lane position.

question: A solid yellow X shown above a reversible lane means:
options: a:You may drive normally in this lane.,b:The lane signal is about to change to a red X; clear the lane.,c:The signal is about to change to a green arrow.,d:The lane is open only for turning.
note: A steady yellow X over a reversible lane means the lane is about to close to traffic in your direction and will soon show a red X. You should safely move out of that lane as soon as possible.

question: How does smoking while driving affect driving?
options: a:Helps maintain driver alertness.,b:Is a distracting activity.,c:Does not affect driving abilities.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it can take one or both hands off the wheel, your eyes off the road, and your attention away from driving. Any activity that interferes with your control of the vehicle or your ability to observe traffic and road conditions increases your risk of a collision.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Passing is always allowed at full speed.,b:Fines are always the same as under normal conditions.,c:You must Slow for the Cone Zone and obey work zone signs and reduced speeds.,d:You only need to slow if workers are visible.
note: In roadwork zones you must slow down, obey all work zone signs, and follow any reduced speed limits. Work zones often have lane shifts, workers close to traffic, and unexpected hazards, so reducing speed and being prepared to stop is essential for everyone’s safety.

question: An octagonal (8-sided) traffic sign always indicates what?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A speed advisory.,c:A hospital.
note: An octagonal (8‑sided) sign shape is reserved exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you constantly pass slower vehicles on a two-lane road, what is likely to happen?
options: a:Improve fuel efficiency.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.,d:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.
note: Frequently passing slower vehicles on a two‑lane road increases your chances of a collision because you must move into the oncoming traffic lane, where your margin for error is small. Each pass creates risk from limited visibility, misjudging the speed or distance of oncoming vehicles, and unexpected actions by the vehicles you are passing. It is safer to pass only when truly necessary and when you have a clear, legal passing zone and enough distance to complete the maneuver safely.

question: If you stop on the roadside at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use parking lights only.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers and leave low-beam headlights on.
note: If you must stop on the roadside at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low‑beam headlights on so other drivers can see you. Low beams and hazard lights make your vehicle visible without creating excessive glare, reducing the chance that another driver will collide with your parked vehicle.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:Alertness and concentration.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, and make it harder to stay alert and focused. Because all of these skills are essential for safe driving, any impairment greatly increases crash risk.

question: What is a likely symptom of a failing vehicle suspension?
options: a:Play (slack) in the steering wheel.,b:Loud squealing brakes.,c:Problems controlling the vehicle or excessive bouncing.
note: The suspension keeps your tires in contact with the road and helps control body movement. When it’s worn, the vehicle may bounce excessively after bumps and feel harder to control, especially in turns or at higher speeds.

question: How quickly does the average body process alcohol?
options: a:Two alcoholic drinks an hour.,b:Three alcoholic drinks an hour.,c:One alcoholic drink an hour.
note: Most people’s bodies can only process about one standard drink per hour. Drinking faster than this causes alcohol to build up in your system, increasing your blood alcohol concentration and impairment.

question: What will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Fresh air and exercise.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Only the passage of time.
note: Nothing speeds sobering up other than time; coffee, fresh air, or other measures do not reduce blood alcohol content.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,b:Engage the vehicle’s four-wheel drive.,c:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: On snow or ice, you should slow down and leave much more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Reduced speed and increased following distance give you more time to react and help prevent skids, even if your vehicle has four‑wheel drive.

question: At a railroad crossing, which of the following should you watch for?
options: a:Vehicles that must stop at all crossings (school buses, hazardous material trucks) and multiple trains.,b:Only one train at a time.,c:Only school buses.
note: At railroad crossings, always look and listen for trains in both directions and be prepared to stop. Some vehicles, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials, must stop at all railroad crossings. Also watch for the possibility of more than one train coming on different tracks.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, drivers:
options: a:Have no right to turn in the arrow direction.,b:Can only go straight through the intersection.,c:Must stop and wait for a solid green light.,d:May turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
