note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. Oncoming traffic and conflicting pedestrians should be stopped, but you must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection or still clearing it before you complete your turn.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass and bicyclists may need extra space to avoid hazards.,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way.,c:You are always moving slower than the bicycle.,d:Bicyclists must yield to all vehicles.
note: Use extra caution when passing a bicycle because you may need to move farther into the opposing lane to give the cyclist safe space. A bicyclist might swerve to avoid potholes, debris, or opening car doors, and oncoming drivers may not anticipate you pulling out to pass. Always ensure you have enough clear distance and time to pass safely without endangering the bicyclist or conflicting with oncoming traffic.

question: As you enter a roundabout, whom should you yield to?
options: a:Only the vehicles in the roundabout.,b:Only pedestrians at the entrance.,c:Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing and all traffic already in the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing at the entrances and exits, and also to all vehicles already circulating within the roundabout. Do not enter until there is a safe gap in traffic and all crossing pedestrians and bicyclists have cleared your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell drivers?
options: a:The speed you must always drive regardless of conditions.,b:Potential or suggested driving speeds for the area.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,d:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must adjust your speed below the posted limit when weather, traffic, road conditions, or visibility make the posted speed unsafe.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign typically indicates:
options: a:Stop.,b:Regulatory sign.,c:Warning.,d:Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, merging traffic, or road work, so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: In traffic moving at 50–55 mph, how can you reduce accident likelihood?
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than others.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than others.,c:Stay within that speed range and flow with other traffic.
note: Driving at about the same speed as surrounding traffic, while staying within the posted speed limit, reduces lane changes and conflicts with other drivers, which lowers the chance of a collision.

question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:
options: a:All vehicles travel at the same speed.,b:Traffic lights always work.,c:One lane of traffic is going in the same direction.,d:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Collisions are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or slower than the surrounding traffic, because speed differences cause sudden braking, lane changes, and misjudged gaps.

question: A center line that is a broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,b:Only allowed during daylight hours.,c:Not permitted from either direction.,d:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. Drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass because it is less safe.

question: You are about to turn right and a pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross. You should:
options: a:Pass in front of them slowly.,b:Turn off your engine until they finish crossing.,c:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,d:Wait until the person has crossed before making your turn.
note: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way. Stop and wait until they have completely crossed and are safely out of your path before you turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you are one vehicle length ahead.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed clearly in your rearview mirror and you have enough space to return safely. This helps avoid cutting the other driver off and reduces the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Any amount of alcohol in a driver's blood can affect what?
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment, reaction time, and coordination, even if you are below the legal limit. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small impairments increase your crash risk.

question: A pedestrian began crossing after the 'Don't Walk' started flashing and is in the road when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing before proceeding.,b:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,c:Honk to make them hurry.,d:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
note: At a green light you must yield to people already in the intersection. Wait until the pedestrian has cleared the roadway before moving.

question: When you need to change lanes, what steps are important?
options: a:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:All of the above.,d:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.
note: A safe lane change requires three key steps: signal well in advance to communicate your intentions, check your mirrors and blind spot to be sure no vehicle is hidden beside you, and make sure the lane is clear and there is enough space before you move over smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:Whoever signals first.
note: At an open or uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:They are in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists generally must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. They must stop at red lights and stop signs, obey speed limits where applicable, and follow right‑of‑way rules. If a bicyclist disobeys these laws, they can be stopped and ticketed by law enforcement just like a motorist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:During the night.,b:Under ideal conditions.,c:During the day.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you may legally drive in ideal conditions, such as good weather, dry roads, and light traffic. You must slow down below the posted limit when conditions are poor, visibility is reduced, or traffic is heavy.

question: After several beers, the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol is:
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Exercising vigorously.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.,d:Waiting several hours.
note: Time is the only reliable method for alcohol to leave the body. Coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed alcohol elimination.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles stopped for no reason.,b:Stop,c:Look to the sides of your vehicle to check for approaching traffic and pedestrians.
note: Intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings are places where vehicles, trains, and pedestrians can cross your path. You should always look carefully to the sides and ahead for people, trains, and other vehicles before proceeding, even if you have the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions by clearly assigning the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a yield sign, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Slow down but never stop under any circumstances.,b:Only yield to vehicles on your right.,c:Yield the right-of-way to close enough cross traffic that would cause a conflict.
note: At a yield sign you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let any traffic, including pedestrians and bicycles, go first if they are close enough that entering would force them to slow, stop, or change lanes. Only proceed when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

question: True or false: Drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.
options: a:True,b:Only at marked crosswalks.,c:Only when children present.,d:False
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and in many unmarked crosswalks at intersections. If a pedestrian is in the crosswalk on your side of the road or close enough to be in danger, you must slow or stop to let them cross safely. Therefore, the statement that drivers are not required to yield is false.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do with the brakes?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly at high speed.,b:Avoid braking; stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, sudden braking usually makes the skid worse. Take your foot off the accelerator and avoid slamming on the brakes. Look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, and brake gently only if needed and if you can do so without locking the wheels (or let ABS work with firm, steady pressure).

question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do about following distance?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Maintain the same distance as in dry conditions.,d:Tailgate the vehicle ahead to control traffic.
note: In rain, snow, fog, or other poor conditions, it takes longer to see hazards and to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. A larger gap reduces the chance of rear‑end collisions on slippery roads.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to you.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: At crosswalks, drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in the crosswalk or about to enter it, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked at an intersection, unless a traffic signal clearly gives the right‑of‑way to vehicles. Slowing or stopping for pedestrians helps ensure they can cross safely.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, how should you proceed?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes if a door opens.
note: When passing a recently parked vehicle, you should assume someone might open a door or step out unexpectedly. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space, and be ready to brake or steer smoothly around any sudden movement. This defensive approach helps prevent dooring crashes and protects pedestrians.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, how should you drive?
options: a:Proceed normally.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop. Do not honk or rush past. Give them plenty of time and space to cross safely, because they rely on sound and predictable driver behavior.

question: Which statement is correct about changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and over your left shoulder for a left lane change in addition to using mirrors.,b:You only need to look in your mirrors.,c:Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, an area your mirrors cannot cover. Never rely only on mirrors, and remember that all vehicles have blind spots, even with multiple mirrors.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Generally safe if brief.,b:Something that rarely happens.,c:Behavior that is extremely risky and takes attention from driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving, such as texting, eating, or adjusting controls. It is extremely risky because it reduces your ability to see hazards, react in time, and control the vehicle, greatly increasing the chance of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following has the highest authority and must be obeyed over the others?
options: a:A steady red traffic light.,b:A stop sign.,c:A police officer directing traffic.
note: If a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, you must follow their directions even if traffic lights or signs say something different. Their instructions override signals, stop signs, and pavement markings because they are managing special situations like crashes, road work, or emergencies.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers.,b:Human error.,c:Bad weather.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, misjudging gaps or speed, following too closely, or failing to yield. While weather and road conditions can contribute, driver decisions and mistakes are the primary cause of most collisions.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights repeatedly.,b:Sound a sharp blast on your horn as a warning.,c:Start to prepare to slow down only.,d:Speed up to pass before the child moves.
note: If a child looks like they may run into the street, you must immediately cover the brake, slow or stop, and be ready to steer away if needed. Use a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child, but never rely only on the horn—always be prepared to stop to avoid hitting a pedestrian.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must drivers do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.,c:Stop on undivided roads in both directions; on divided highways, stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in both directions must stop on undivided roads. On a divided highway with a physical median or barrier, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; oncoming traffic usually may proceed with caution. Always know your state’s specific rules, but never pass a bus that is loading or unloading children on your side of the road.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted when it is safe.
note: A broken yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken on your side, you may pass another vehicle if there is no oncoming traffic and you can complete the pass safely and legally. If visibility or conditions are poor, you should not pass even if the line is broken.

question: May only vehicles with special plates or placards for persons with disabilities park in spaces reserved for them?
options: a:Only if the driver has a permit displayed.,b:Only on weekends.,c:True,d:False
note: Accessible parking spaces are reserved for vehicles displaying valid disability plates or placards, and they must be used only when transporting the person with the disability. Having a plate or placard does not give permission to park there if the qualified person is not being picked up, dropped off, or riding in the vehicle.

question: Which behavior is part of defensive driving?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to look for hazards.,b:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,c:Look only at the car directly in front of you.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and checking mirrors so you can spot hazards early and react in time. Staring only at the area directly in front of your vehicle reduces your ability to see developing problems and is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your lane when:
options: a:You hear the other driver honk.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting them off or causing a rear-end collision.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Even over-the-counter and prescription drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many drugs—illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter—can slow your reactions, affect judgment, or make you drowsy. Even if a drug is legal or prescribed, it is unsafe and illegal to drive if it impairs your ability to operate a vehicle safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Honk repeatedly to warn the other driver.,b:Re-enter the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.
note: Before passing, you must check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear, then signal to show your intention. Only move into the passing lane when it is safe, and return to your original lane only after you have safely cleared the other vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:
options: a:Make a U-turn at the intersection instead.,b:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,d:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn when you reach an intersection, continue straight and go to the next intersection. Making sudden lane changes or turns from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,c:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe.
note: A single broken yellow center line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed in both directions when it can be done safely and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

question: True or false: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
options: a:False,b:True,c:Only at marked crosswalks.,d:Only at signalized intersections.
note: Drivers must often yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections, but pedestrians do not always have the right-of-way. For example, pedestrians must obey traffic signals and should not suddenly leave a curb into the path of a vehicle that cannot stop in time.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on your brakes and stop immediately.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force back onto the pavement.,c:Ease off the gas, slow down, and gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep steering straight. Do not jerk the wheel or slam on the brakes. After you have slowed and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement. Abrupt steering or hard braking can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: Which of the following is true regarding railroad crossings?
options: a:You must stop when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,b:You always have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing.,c:You should speed across if no train is visible.,d:You never need to stop for a crossing without lights.
note: At railroad crossings, you must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or active warning devices (flashing lights, gates, or bells) indicate a train is approaching. Even when you are not required to stop, you must slow, look, and listen for trains and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Wearing both the lap belt and the shoulder belt in a two-part system increases protection. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Using both the lap belt and shoulder belt keeps you better restrained in a crash. The lap belt holds your lower body in place, and the shoulder belt helps protect your head and chest. Wearing only one part greatly reduces the protection and can increase the risk of serious injury.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection at a normal, safe speed. Do not stop suddenly in the intersection and do not accelerate aggressively; your goal is to leave the intersection safely and smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street?
options: a:Any lane so long as it looks safe.,b:The center lane.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you must begin your turn from the lane closest to the left curb. This position lines you up correctly for the turn, reduces conflicts with other traffic, and is required by standard lane-use rules.

question: Before changing lanes, which check should you perform?
options: a:Check your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.,c:Check your rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, you must quickly turn your head to check over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where mirrors cannot. Use your mirrors first to judge traffic, then do a quick head check just before moving into the new lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Ignore pedestrians in the crosswalk.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk. Pedestrians in the intersection have the right-of-way, and you must wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding or turning.

question: Which of these does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance is the sum of your reaction distance and braking distance. It depends on your reaction time, vehicle speed, brake and tire condition, road surface, and visibility. The time of day by itself does not determine how far it takes you to stop; it is the actual conditions (like darkness or weather) and your speed and alertness that matter.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only if a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or a guide dog are visually impaired and have special legal protection. You must always yield the right-of-way to them, whether they are in a crosswalk, at an intersection, or stepping off the curb. Be prepared to stop completely and do not honk or try to hurry them.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using lights or a siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane until it passes.,c:Pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one-handed and talking to a passenger), you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them.,b:Give the vehicle extra space.,c:Avoid following the driver's example.,d:Know the driver is reducing their safety margin by being inattentive.
note: A distracted driver is more likely to make sudden or unpredictable moves. The safest response is to increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react if they brake suddenly, drift, or miss traffic signals. Giving extra space reduces your risk of a rear-end collision or needing an emergency maneuver.

question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep wheels straight ahead.,b:Turn your wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels toward the curb or side of the road.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will rest against the curb or edge instead of rolling into traffic.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: On a two-lane road with no physical divider, all drivers in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. Remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road from either side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When turning left into a driveway.,b:When the car ahead is disabled.,c:When doing so would interfere with traffic or be unsafe.
note: A single broken white or yellow line may be crossed to pass or change lanes only when it is clearly safe and will not interfere with other traffic. If crossing the line would force other drivers to brake or swerve, or if visibility or road conditions make it unsafe, you must not cross.

question: What do round traffic signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:School zones.,b:An upcoming railroad crossing.,c:No passing zones.
note: In the U.S., round traffic signs are used specifically to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see a round yellow railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it important to always use your turn signal?
options: a:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,d:All of the above.
note: Turn signals must be used any time you change where your vehicle is going in traffic: when pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area, when changing lanes, and when pulling into or out of a parking space. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your movements and helps prevent collisions.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which substance?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Amphetamines.,c:Anger.
note: Driving while very tired can affect you much like alcohol: slower reaction time, poor judgment, and drifting out of your lane. Being awake for a long period can impair driving ability to a level similar to having alcohol in your system, so you should never drive when severely fatigued.

question: Which statement about backing your vehicle is true?
options: a:Backing is safe if you drive slowly.,b:Backing is never dangerous with mirrors.,c:Backing is only dangerous for large vehicles.,d:Backing is always dangerous because rear visibility is limited.
note: Backing is always risky because you cannot see as well behind your vehicle, even with mirrors or cameras. You should back slowly, check around your vehicle before moving, and, when needed, turn and look over your shoulder or use a spotter to make sure the path is clear.

question: How are reversible lanes usually marked?
options: a:Single dashed white lines.,b:Single solid white lines.,c:Double dashed yellow lines.,d:Double solid red lines.
note: Reversible lanes are typically separated from adjacent lanes by broken (dashed) white lines, just like other lanes going in the same direction. What makes them reversible is the overhead lane-use control signals (green arrow, red X) that tell you whether you may use the lane at a given time, not special double dashed yellow markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the speed limit and create a backup of traffic, you should:
options: a:Should not let following cars pass.,b:Must pull off the road and let other vehicles pass.,c:Always has the right-of-way.,d:Is a very safe driver.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes sudden braking and risky passing. If you are moving well below the speed limit and creating a line of vehicles behind you, you are generally required to pull off the road at a safe place and let other vehicles pass when possible.

question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:At all times.,c:Unless you do not see any children present.,d:Only when police are present.
note: Drivers must always obey school crossing guards whenever they are on duty and giving directions. Their instructions have the same legal force as standard traffic control devices and are meant to protect children and other pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After you pass another vehicle traveling the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:About three seconds after passing.,b:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and you have enough space to return without cutting them off. This ensures you have fully cleared the other vehicle and can merge back safely.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what is the recommended recovery?
options: a:Accelerate to regain control.,b:Stop where you are and call for help.,c:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,d:Reduce speed
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually while keeping the vehicle straight. Once you have reduced speed and checked for traffic, gently steer back onto the roadway. Jerking the wheel or turning sharply at high speed can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: Why is following a motorcycle too closely dangerous?
options: a:Because motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.,b:Because motorcycles always have the right-of-way.,c:Because motorcycles do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,d:Because a motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and often have very effective brakes, so they can stop more quickly than many cars. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcycle stops suddenly, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles.

question: True or false: How fast you drive does not affect the distance your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:It depends on the vehicle's weight.,b:True.,c:Only in wet conditions.,d:False.
note: Your speed has a major effect on stopping distance. The faster you drive, the farther your vehicle will travel from the moment you see a hazard to the moment you come to a complete stop. Both reaction distance and braking distance increase with speed, so higher speeds always require more space to stop safely.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Drive past the bus if no children are visible.,b:Pass slowly on the left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,d:Honk your horn before passing.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing the road and may be hard to see. Never pass a bus in this situation unless a specific lawfully marked divided highway exception applies in your state.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the statewide speed limit in school zones (unless otherwise posted)?
options: a:10 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:20 mph.,d:25 mph.
note: School zone speed limits are set by each state and local jurisdiction; there is no single statewide or nationwide default that is always 15 mph. Many states use 15, 20, 25, or other speeds depending on the area and posted signs. Drivers must obey the specific speed limit posted on school zone signs rather than assuming one standard number.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't impair driving?
options: a:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,b:Drive within your physical limitations.,c:Keep physically fit and have regular physical exams.,d:All of the above.
note: Safe driving depends on your overall physical condition, including how medications, fatigue, illness, or long-term health issues affect you. To reduce risk, you should know how any medicine affects your driving, stay within your physical limits, and have regular checkups to monitor your fitness to drive. All of these actions together help ensure your condition will not impair your driving.

question: If you must drive in foggy conditions, you should:
options: a:Use your high beams to see farther ahead.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.,c:Use your low beam headlights.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and drive fast.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead, and increase following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic ahead is blocking an intersection you should:
options: a:Honk to make the traffic move forward.,b:Enter the intersection if the light is green to avoid blocking others.,c:Pull alongside the vehicle in front of you.,d:Wait to enter the intersection until you can clear it completely.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Blocking the intersection can prevent cross traffic from moving when their light turns green and is illegal in many states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often,b:Only at uncontrolled intersections.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.,d:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
note: Right-of-way is something you yield, not something you take. Even if you are legally entitled to go first, you should yield whenever doing so helps prevent a collision. Never assume other drivers will follow the rules or yield correctly.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Proceed if no children are visible.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,d:Slow to 10 mph and pass carefully.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing in front of or behind the bus.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab only.,b:Directly behind the body only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.,d:Along both sides near the cab and directly behind the truck.
note: Large trucks have multiple large blind spots, often called “no-zones.” These are directly behind the truck, along both sides (especially the right side), and sometimes directly in front of the cab. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you. Avoid lingering in these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with a green light but heavy oncoming traffic, what may you do?
options: a:Immediately back out of the intersection.,b:Enter the intersection and wait for a safe gap to complete your left turn.,c:Ignore oncoming traffic and make the turn.,d:Turn from any lane available.
note: With a green light and heavy oncoming traffic, you must yield to oncoming vehicles before turning left. You may move into the intersection and wait with your wheels straight until there is a safe gap or the light changes and oncoming traffic stops, then complete your turn.

question: Hydroplaning is most often caused by:
options: a:Excessive stops.,b:Sudden turns.,c:Driving too fast for wet conditions.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a layer of water and lose contact with the road. This is most likely at higher speeds in wet conditions, so driving too fast for the amount of water on the road greatly increases the risk.

question: How should you check a blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the side mirror.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder toward the lane you will enter.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter. This head check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover, helping you avoid vehicles riding alongside you.

question: Is it lawful to drive through, around, or under railroad crossing gates or barriers?
options: a:False — you must never drive through or under railroad gates.,b:True — you may if no train is visible.
note: You must never drive through, around, or under lowered or lowering railroad gates, even if you do not see a train. Gates and flashing signals mean a train is approaching, and ignoring them is both illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway?
options: a:40 mph.,b:There is no single nationwide default; obey the posted limit.,c:55 mph.
note: Speed limits on rural interstate highways are set by each state and commonly range from 65 to 80 mph. There is no single nationwide default of 75 mph. Always follow the posted speed limit signs for the specific road and state you are driving in.

question: When backing up your vehicle you should:
options: a:Look through the rear window.,b:Press hard on the gas pedal.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,d:Use only your side mirrors.
note: When backing, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see the area behind you. Mirrors alone leave blind spots and may not show small children, objects, or hazards directly behind the vehicle.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign — stop completely and proceed when safe.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What effect does even a small amount of alcohol have on driving skills?
options: a:Alcohol improves driving ability.,b:Only amounts above the legal limit have any effect.,c:Even small amounts reduce concentration
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reaction time, reduce concentration, and affect judgment. There is no amount of alcohol that is safe for driving, even if you are below the legal limit.

question: After a minor intersection crash with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Never move the vehicle for any reason.,b:Leave the vehicle where it is until law enforcement arrives.,c:If possible, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane to a safe location.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries, if your vehicle is drivable and it is safe to do so, you should move it out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe location. This helps prevent additional collisions and reduces traffic congestion.

question: Is it legal to pass across double solid yellow center lines? True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Double solid yellow center lines mean no passing in either direction. You must not cross them to pass another vehicle. They may only be crossed when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when specifically allowed by law, but never for passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You come to an intersection showing a flashing red light. You should:
options: a:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,b:Slow and proceed if clear.,c:Ignore it if no cross traffic is present.,d:Come to a full stop
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop regardless of traffic.,b:Yield only to vehicles coming from your right.,c:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield to traffic and pedestrians close enough to be a hazard.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right‑of‑way to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard. If no traffic is close enough to cause a conflict, you may proceed without stopping.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it necessary to use the parking brake?
options: a:True — you do not need to set the parking brake.,b:False — you should set your parking brake and turn on your hazard flashers.
note: When you make an emergency roadside stop, you should secure your vehicle so it cannot roll. Set the parking brake and, if on a slope, turn the wheels appropriately. Turn on your hazard flashers so other drivers can see your stopped vehicle in time to avoid it.

question: A flashing yellow X above a reversible lane indicates:
options: a:Drivers may use this lane to travel normally.,b:The lane may be used only to complete a left turn.,c:The signal is about to change to a red X.,d:The lane is open for merging.
note: On roads with reversible lanes, a flashing yellow X above a lane means you may use that lane only to make left turns. It is not open for through traffic; enter it only when you are preparing for and completing a left turn.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,c:Decreases your field of vision.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows, creating a “tunnel vision” effect. This makes it harder to see pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles approaching from the sides, so you must scan more actively and adjust your speed to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Force other cars to make room for them.,b:Always have the right-of-way.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp before merging.
note: On entrance ramps, you must adjust your speed and position so you can merge smoothly into traffic already on the interstate. Vehicles on the freeway have the right-of-way, so you must yield to them and only merge when there is a safe gap.

question: At an intersection, what does a flashing red light require you to do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:You do not have to stop if the way is clear.,c:Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or approaching the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct practice for slowing on a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Keep your speed constant once on the ramp.,b:Wait to slow down until you are actually on the exit ramp, then reduce speed as needed.,c:Brake hard before entering the ramp.
note: On a freeway, keep up with the flow of traffic until you are in the exit lane and on the ramp. Do not slow suddenly on the main freeway, as this can cause rear-end collisions. Once on the ramp, gradually reduce speed to match any posted advisory speed for the ramp.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, whom should you yield to?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles present before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over a lane if it is safe to do so.,b:Always remain at your present speed regardless of merging traffic.,c:Speed up to prevent congestion.,d:Honk at the entering driver.
note: When you see a merging traffic sign, be prepared for vehicles entering your lane. If possible, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed slightly to create a safe gap so merging drivers can enter smoothly.

question: How can you help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance?
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed.,b:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Frequently tapping your brakes to signal them.,d:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: You help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance by driving predictably: maintain a steady speed and signal early before slowing or turning. Sudden speed changes or brake tapping can confuse or startle other drivers and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: What is the effect of slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events?
options: a:It prevents rear-end collisions.,b:It improves traffic flow.,c:It causes additional traffic congestion.
note: Slowing down just to look at a collision or unusual event (rubbernecking) disrupts traffic flow, creates backups, and increases the risk of additional crashes. You should focus on the road ahead and continue at a safe, steady speed unless you are required to slow or stop.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Make you drowsy while driving.,b:Cause your car to use more oil.,c:Increase engine power.,d:Improve fuel efficiency.
note: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide and other fumes enter the vehicle. These gases can make you drowsy, impair your judgment, and in high concentrations can cause unconsciousness or death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only where road signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and it is safe to do so.,b:Within an intersection if you see no oncoming vehicles.,c:On a curve if you have a clear view ahead.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and where you have enough clear space and visibility to complete the pass without speeding or cutting back in too closely. You should not pass in intersections, on hills, or on curves where your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Watch out for standing water or puddles.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Use cruise control to maintain traction.,d:Keep your tires properly maintained.
note: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to slow down when roads are wet or slushy, especially at higher speeds where tires can ride up on a film of water. Proper tire maintenance and watching for standing water also help, but reducing speed is the most important factor in maintaining traction.

question: Which action helps reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Use your horn frequently.
note: To reduce road rage, drive predictably and courteously. Always signal before changing lanes so other drivers know what you intend to do. Avoid distracting behaviors like talking on a cell phone and do not use your horn unnecessarily, as these can irritate other drivers and increase tension on the road.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Allow extra space if you are behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a motorcycle.,c:Follow at the same distance as you would any other car.,d:Allow extra space when following a station wagon.
note: When following a motorcycle, increase your following distance. Motorcycles are smaller, harder to see, and can stop or swerve more quickly than cars. Leaving extra space in front of your vehicle gives you more time to react if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.,b:Only in front of your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle — front, rear, and sides.
note: A space cushion is the open space around your vehicle that gives you time to react. You should keep space on all sides—front, rear, and sides—whenever possible. This extra room helps you avoid collisions if another driver makes a mistake or a hazard appears suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right-of-way to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection or close enough to be a hazard. Proceed only when it is safe and you will not interfere with other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permissible to drive off the road to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes — if there are two or more lanes going your direction.,b:Yes — if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:No — you may not drive off the paved portion or onto the shoulder to pass.
note: You may not drive off the paved or main-traveled portion of the roadway or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Passing must be done within a legal lane of travel. Driving onto the shoulder is unsafe and illegal because it reduces control and can endanger stopped or slow-moving vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed in a business or residential area?
options: a:45 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:35 mph.,d:30 mph.
note: In many U.S. jurisdictions, the default speed limit in business and residential areas is 30 mph unless signs show a different limit. Always follow posted signs, as local laws can set lower or higher limits.

question: What is true about bicyclists and traffic laws?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws.,b:They have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers and can be ticketed.,c:They always receive a warning instead of a citation.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and they can receive citations for violations just like drivers.

question: A broken yellow centerline means:
options: a:You may pass on the right only.,b:Passing is never permitted in either direction.,c:You must stay in your lane at all times.,d:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may cross it to pass another vehicle on the left only when the lane is clear and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane, you should:
options: a:Only check your mirrors and change lanes quickly.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Signal and move without checking blind spots.,d:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Before moving from the left lane to the right lane, check your mirrors, signal your intention, and then look over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when the lane is clear and you can move safely.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and do not brake abruptly.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,d:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard or sudden braking, then gently brake when the vehicle is under control and steer to a safe place off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Change lanes while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should never change lanes while you are in an intersection because traffic is crossing from multiple directions and drivers are focusing on signals and right‑of‑way, not on lane changes. Make all lane changes before or after the intersection, and always check mirrors and blind spots first.

question: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, you should:
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,d:Leave your wheels straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back gently until the back of the front tire rests against the curb. This way, if the brakes fail, the car will roll into the curb instead of into traffic. If there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road.

question: Why should you use headlights in rain, snow, or fog?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,d:To improve your radio reception.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, visibility is reduced, so you turn on your headlights—especially low beams—so other drivers can see your vehicle more easily. Many states require headlights whenever wipers are in use. High beams can reflect off fog or heavy precipitation and make it harder to see, so use low beams.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Block them from changing lanes.,b:Remain calm and move out of their way rather than retaliating.,c:Immediately pursue and confront the driver.,d:Flash your lights to show them they are wrong.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm, slow slightly if needed, and create space rather than trying to block, chase, or confront them. Retaliating or engaging with an aggressive driver greatly increases the risk of a crash or road‑rage incident.

question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only when all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Change lanes.,c:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
note: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop and remain stopped until you are sure all pedestrians have safely crossed. Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, because pedestrians may be in front of that vehicle where you cannot see them.

question: How should you handle turns on slick roads?
options: a:Accelerate through the turn.,b:Change lanes quickly before the turn.,c:Enter turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slick or slippery roads, you should slow down before entering a turn so your tires can maintain traction. Entering the turn more slowly and steering smoothly helps prevent skids and loss of control.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,d:Pass the bus cautiously without stopping.
note: After a school bus unloads children and you are legally allowed to proceed, move slowly and be prepared to stop. Children may walk along the side of the road or suddenly cross in front of you, so you must watch carefully in all directions.

question: A driver does not need to leave as much following distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must leave at least as much, and often more, following distance behind a motorcycle than behind a car. Motorcycles can stop very quickly and are harder to see, so a following distance of at least three to four seconds gives you time to react safely.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Call the police only.,b:Stop.,c:Determine if anyone is injured and leave the scene if damage is minor.,d:Stop only.
note: If you are involved in a serious crash, you must stop immediately. Once stopped, check for injuries, call emergency services, and stay at the scene. Never leave the scene of a crash, especially when there are injuries or significant damage.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop driving and rest.,b:Open your window and continue driving.,c:Drink coffee and drive on.,d:Turn on the radio loudly.
note: When you start to feel tired while driving, the safest choice is to stop driving and rest or change drivers. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee do not reliably prevent fatigue-related crashes.

question: What should you do with your speed when making a turn?
options: a:Increase to clear the turn quickly.,b:Maintain the same speed as before the turn.,c:Adjust your speed (slow to maintain control).
note: When turning, you should slow to a safe speed before the turn and maintain enough control to stay in your lane and react to hazards. Entering a turn too fast can cause skidding or drifting out of your lane.

question: When you see a Reduced speed 35 mph sign, what does it mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the sign.,b:The reduced speed zone begins at the next posted speed sign.,c:You have a long distance to slow down before the reduced zone.
note: A reduced speed sign means the new speed limit starts exactly at the sign. You must already be slowing so that you are at or below the posted speed as you reach the sign, not farther down the road.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow on a signal mean for turning traffic?
options: a:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b:You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.,c:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,d:The arrow means left turns are always prohibited.
note: A steady yellow arrow tells you the protected turn phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians if you proceed.

question: Which safety restraint combination is most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,c:Neither will improve survival.,d:Only a lap and shoulder belt.
note: Seat belts greatly increase survival and reduce injury. Airbags provide extra protection when used in combination with a lap and shoulder belt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:If there is no oncoming traffic.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is not allowed in either direction. You may only cross it for limited reasons, such as turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: Must you yield to children playing in the street?
options: a:Only in school zones.,b:Only if a parent is present.,c:True,d:False
note: You must always be prepared to yield to children in or near the street, regardless of whether it is a school zone or whether an adult is present. Children can act unpredictably, so you should slow down, be ready to stop, and give them the right-of-way whenever they are in or entering the roadway.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The color of your vehicle.,b:The condition of the road and surface traction.,c:The time of day.,d:Signal lights ahead.
note: Stopping distance depends heavily on how much traction your tires have on the road surface. Wet, icy, snowy, or gravel-covered roads greatly increase the distance it takes to stop, so you must slow down and increase following distance in poor conditions.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:Red curb indicates a fire zone with parking restrictions.,b:Blue curb indicates disabled parking.,c:White curb indicates no parking.
note: Painted curbs use standard colors to show parking rules. A red curb typically means no stopping, standing, or parking—often for fire lanes or emergency access. Blue is for disabled parking with a valid placard or plate, and white or yellow may indicate limited-time or loading zones depending on local rules.

question: How might a crosswalk be indicated?
options: a:Always indicated by horizontal pavement markings.,b:Marked or unmarked—both exist.,c:Always unmarked.
note: A crosswalk can be either marked or unmarked. Marked crosswalks have painted lines or other pavement markings. Unmarked crosswalks typically exist at intersections where sidewalks would naturally continue across the street. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks.

question: Roads and streets are most slippery under which condition?
options: a:When they are clean and dry.,b:After it has been raining hard for several hours.,c:Just after it starts to rain.,d:Only when snow is present.
note: Roads are often most slippery just after it starts to rain. Water lifts oil, grease, and other residues to the surface, creating a slick layer that reduces traction. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves, though you should still drive carefully.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are stopped and given a citation.,c:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
note: Drivers must carry proof of financial responsibility (usually an insurance card) whenever they drive. Law enforcement can require you to show this proof if you are stopped for a traffic violation or if you are involved in a collision. Failing to provide proof when requested can result in citations and other penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.
